state:
On or about XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a complaint with the CFPB regarding the improper reporting of a credit account on my credit report by PYOD LLC who was attempting to collect an alleged debt for an account I formerly held with XXXX XXXX XXXX. The outcome of that complaint resulted in the removal of PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) from all of my credit reports. After further consideration of the laws afforded to me as a federally protected person, PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) and XXXX XXXX XXXX  owe me remedies, as afforded to me through federal and state law, for improperly reporting my credit account to the three Credit Reporting Agencies ( XXXX  ), XXXX ( a non-affiliate ), XXXX ( a non-affiliate ), and XXXX ( a non-affiliate ) ; sharing my personal information between XXXX XXXX XXXX, the XXXX  ( non-affiliates ) and PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) without my expressed written consent ; selling my personal information without my written consent to a non-affiliate ( i.e. PYOD LLC ) ; misrepresentation of facts by alleging and communicating to me that a debt was owed to PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) on behalf of XXXX XXXX XXXX  when PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) willingly and knowingly " purchased the debt '' from XXXX XXXX XXXX thus nullifying any alleged debt to XXXX XXXX XXXX ; and, damaging my credit report and credit reporting history by reporting this alleged debt to the XXXX  which misrepresented my creditworthiness and caused me financial and material damages as it prevented me from obtaining a more favorable credit rating ultimately resulting in me being denied credit, having a lower available credit line, and/or having a higher interest rate on certain lines of credit. The specific violations of law committed by PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) and XXXX XXXX XXXX  are, but are not limited to : The Privacy Act of 1974 and 15 USC 1681 ( 4 ) which states that I have the right to privacy.

15 USC 1681 which states that there must be a permissible purpose for this information to be shared 15 USC 1681a which provides for the definitions and rules of construction where specifically subsection ( d ) Consumer Report. 
( XXXX ) In general.The term consumer report means any written, oral, or other communication of any information by a consumer reporting agency bearing on a consumers credit worthiness, credit standing, credit capacity, character, general reputation, personal characteristics, or mode of living which is used or expected to be used or collected in whole or in part for the purpose of serving as a factor in establishing the consumers eligibility for ( A ) credit or insurance to be used primarily for personal, family, or household purposes ; ( B ) employment purposes ; or ( C ) any other purpose authorized under section 1681b of this title. 
( XXXX ) Exclusions.Except as provided in paragraph ( XXXX ), the term consumer report does not include ( A ) subject to section 1681s3 of this title, any ( i ) report containing information solely as to transactions or experiences between the consumer and the person making the report ; ( ii ) communication of that information among persons related by common ownership or affiliated by corporate control ; or ( iii ) communication of other information among persons related by common ownership or affiliated by corporate control, if it is clearly and conspicuously disclosed to the consumer that the information may be communicated among such persons and the consumer is given the opportunity, before the time that the information is initially communicated, to direct that such information not be communicated among such persons ; ( B ) any authorization or approval of a specific extension of credit directly or indirectly by the issuer of a credit card or similar device ; ( C ) any report in which a person who has been requested by a third party to make a specific extension of credit directly or indirectly to a consumer conveys his or her decision with respect to such request, if the third party advises the consumer of the name and address of the person to whom the request was made, and such person makes the disclosures to the consumer required under section 1681m of this title... Both XXXX XXXX XXXX  and PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) failed to meet and/or adhere to any of these definitions and violated my federally protected rights when they engaged in a monetary transaction to buy and sell my personal and financial information.

15 USC 1681b which states that there must exist a permissible purpose and that ( a ) In general, subject to subsection ( c ), any consumer reporting agency may furnish a consumer report under the following circumstances and no other : ( XXXX ) In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer to whom it relates. Neither XXXX XXXX XXXX nor PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) obtained my written instructions. 

15 U.S. Code 1681q - Obtaining information under false pretenses - In the attached letter from XXXX XXXX XXXX, it states that XXXX  XXXX had no knowledge of how PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) obtained my information nor that they were attempting to collect any alleged debt from me. However, in PYOD LLC 's ( a non-affiliate ) response letter to the complaint filed with the CFPB on or about XX/XX/XXXX, PYOD LLC asserts that they " purchased '' the " debt '' from " XXXX XXXX XXXX ''. Thus, the two ( 2 ) letters conflict in how PYOD LLC obtained my personal information which was under XXXX XXXX 's fiduciary and material care from approximately XXXX to XXXX. This also means that PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) may have obtained my personal information under false pretenses and/or stole my information from XXXX XXXX XXXX , and/or XXXX XXXX XXXX was negligent in protecting my personal information. This also means that either XXXX XXXX Bank and/or PYOD LLC is in violation of 15 USC 1681r , which is punishable by a fine under title 18 and/or no more than 2 years in XXXX. 

! 5 USC 1681 s-3 affiliate sharing. XXXX XXXX XXXX, the XXXX, and PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) have all violated this code as PYOD LLC and the XXXX are non-affiliates to XXXX XXXX XXXX, and one another. None of these companies had the legal right to share my information and violated this code. 

15 USC 1692b Acquisition of location, under abusive debt practices, states Any debt collector communicating with any person other than the consumer for the purpose of acquiring location information about the consumer shall ( 2 ) not state that such consumer owes any debt ; ( 4 ) not communicate by post card ; ( 5 ) not use any language or symbol on any envelope or in the contents of any communication effected by the mails or telegram that indicates that the debt collector is in the debt collection business or that the communication relates to the collection of a debt. PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) did violate this code by committing these acts. 

PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) also violated 15 USC 1692c ( a ) Communication with the consumer which states that generally, Without the prior consent of the consumer given directly to the debt collector or the express permission of a court of competent jurisdiction, a debt collector may not communicate with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt ( b ) Communication with third parties which states ; Except as provided in section 1692b of this title, without the prior consent of the consumer given directly to the debt collector, or the express permission of a court of competent jurisdiction, or as reasonably necessary to effectuate a postjudgment judicial remedy, a debt collector may not communicate, in connection with the collection of any debt, with any person other than the consumer, his attorney, a consumer reporting agency if otherwise permitted by law, the creditor, the attorney of the creditor, or the attorney of the debt collector. PYOD LLC ( a non-affiliate ) violated this code when it reported to the CRAs, my alleged debt with XXXX XXXX XXXX  negatively affecting my credit score and overall creditworthiness. 

PYOD LLC violated 15 U.S. Code 1692e and 15 USC 1681q- False or misleading representations by communicating that they had the legal right to collect any alleged debt on behalf of XXXX  XXXX XXXX XXXX PYOD LLC also violated this code by asserting that a debt was still owed to XXXX XXXX XXXX, when in fact PYOD LLC had purchased the debt making the debt owed to XXXX XXXX XXXX  " void '', " cancelled '', " redeemed '', and/or otherwise " paid in full ''. I had/have no contractual obligation to PYOD LLC and have not, nor am currently engaged in any financial or other transaction with PYOD LLC XXXX Thus PYOD LLC falsely and misleadingly attempted to construct a contract where none existed. 

Due to these numerous violations of my federally protected rights, I am seeking federal and state remedies afforded to me under the governing laws and codes against the aforementioned companies.

I get a response few days later around XX/XX/XXXX that my appeal was denied and the actions taken to close the account would remain with the hold of the XXXX. I made phone calls but no one could help me. The only advise was i needed to wait for the 120 days. In XXXX XXXX I contacted Chase XXXX that the 120 days has passed and please return the XXXX that was held. A week later, I get XXXX emails from Chase XXXX stating as follows XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Chase Integrated Payments ) XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, Thanks for reaching out to us! My name is XXXX, and I am happy to assist you today. 

I can confirm that the 120 days period has already passed from the date the account was closed. I will chime in our Trust and Safety team to confirm if they can now release the funds.

Subject : Complaint Against CHASE CARD SERVICES for Violations of XXXX XXXX, Public Law XXXX, UCC Provisions, Federal Regulations, U.S. Codes, and Unlawful Closure of Accounts Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), I am filing this formal complaint against CHASE CARD SERVICES for numerous violations of my rights, including but not limited to : failure to honor lawful payment instruments, improper retention of securities, violation of XXXX and holder-in-due-course laws, breaches of federal regulations and U.S. Codes, unlawful closure of accounts, and potential theft, fraud, language fraud, and securities fraud. These violations contradict House Joint Resolution XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ), Public Law XXXX ( Emergency Banking Act ), the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), the U.S. Constitution, and various federal laws and regulations. 
Detailed Summary of Violations : Failure to Honor Securities and Lawful Payment Instruments : I tendered lawful payments using securities and negotiable instruments provided by CHASE CARD SERVICES, such as bills, statements, equity checks, bearer bonds, and coupons attached to the statements. According to XXXX XXXX ( a ) and UCC XXXX XXXX a ) ( XXXX ), these instruments are valid as negotiable instruments, and I accepted these securities " for value, '' issuing a restrictive endorsement as outlined in UCC XXXX. Additionally, I affixed postage stamps ( lawful money ) to these securities under XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX ( b ) ( XXXX ), reinforcing my payments. 
Despite receiving these securities through registered and certified mail, CHASE CARD SERVICES failed to discharge the debt, return the securities, or properly credit my account, in violation of XXXX XXXX ( b ). This provision mandates that any obligation is discharged to the extent of a payment made by a negotiable instrument unless that instrument is returned or dishonored. Their retention of the securities without action violates my rights as both a creditor and holder of the instruments. 
Unlawful Closure of Accounts and Definition of " Accounts '' : It is important to clarify that the term account inherently means a place for deposits and withdrawals, not a static or limited financial agreement. As such, CHASE CARD SERVICES unlawfully closed my accounts even after I had discharged the related debts through the lawful tender of securities. These accounts, by their nature, should be considered open-ended credit plans, which should not have a predetermined limit. Under my unlimited right to contract, as protected by the U.S. Constitution, I am entitled to maintain these accounts without arbitrary closure, particularly after meeting my financial obligations through lawful payments. 
The attempt to impose artificial credit limits or close my accounts after the debt was discharged is unlawful. Showing limits on an open-ended credit plan, as CHASE CARD SERVICES has done, is illegal and contrary to both the terms of open-ended credit and contract law principles. Their action constitutes a breach of XXXX XXXX concerning the resolution of debts through accord and satisfaction and violates my constitutional right to contract freely without interference. 
Potential Fraud, Theft, and Securities Fraud : In addition to their mishandling of the securities and failure to honor my lawful payments, I am concerned that CHASE CARD SERVICES may be engaging in fraudulent activities. By retaining the securities I sent, continuing to demand payment for already discharged debts, and unlawfully closing accounts, they may be guilty of theft, securities fraud, and other forms of financial fraud. Their refusal to properly process the negotiable instruments and their subsequent closure of the accounts indicate potential securities fraud under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and related provisions under federal securities laws. 
Language fraud may also be present in the manner in which the terms of my accounts, securities, and payments have been communicated. CHASE CARD SERVICES has used deceptive or unclear language that obscures the nature of my rights and obligations, particularly in regard to the use of lawful money and the nature of the securities provided. By misleading me about the status of the accounts and payments, they are potentially engaging in fraudulent misrepresentation under 18 U.S. Code 1341 ( Mail Fraud ) and 18 U.S. Code 1343 ( Wire Fraud ). 
Violation of Holder-in-Due-Course Laws : As the holder of the securities and negotiable instruments I tendered, I am entitled to the protections and rights outlined in UCC XXXX. A holder in due course has the right to enforce the payment of the instrument free from most claims and defenses. CHASE CARD SERVICES, by refusing to honor my position as the holder of these instruments, has violated my holder-in-due-course rights. They retained the securities without processing them, have continued to unlawfully demand further payments, and have denied my rightful claim to the value of these instruments, in violation of XXXX XXXX ( concerning defenses and claims to an instrument ). 
Violation of U.S. Codes and Federal Regulations : By refusing to process the private instruments I provided, unlawfully retaining my securities, and denying my right to claim them, CHASE CARD SERVICES has violated various U.S. codes, including 12 U.S. Code 411, which governs the issuance and use of lawful money. Additionally, they have breached multiple provisions of the Code of Federal Regulations ( CFR ), particularly those governing the handling of negotiable instruments and securities. The improper handling of these private instruments suggests potential violations of 15 U.S. Code Chapter 41- Consumer Credit Protection. 
Failure to Discharge Debt Under the Emergency Banking Act and Gold Clause : According to Public Law XXXX ( Emergency Banking Act ) and HJR XXXX, all debts must be discharged upon the tender of lawful money. My payment, which consisted of securities and lawful money ( postage stamps ), fully satisfied the obligation. [ Institution Name ] has unlawfully refused to recognize the discharge of my debt, in violation of the Gold Clause, which prohibits the refusal to accept lawful money for the satisfaction of debts. Their continued claims that I owe further payments after I have already tendered lawful payment indicate a violation of both public law and federal monetary statutes. 
Applicable UCC, Federal Regulations, U.S. Codes, and Constitutional Protections : XXXX XXXX ( a ) : Defines a negotiable instrument as an unconditional promise or order to pay a fixed amount of money. 
XXXX XXXX : Governs restrictive endorsements and their legal effect on the instrument. 
XXXX XXXX : Holder-in-due-course rights and their protection in the enforcement of negotiable instruments. 
XXXX XXXX : Outlines claims and defenses to negotiable instruments, including wrongful retention. 
XXXX XXXX : Covers accord and satisfaction, requiring that when a debt is discharged, no further payment can be demanded. 
XXXX XXXX ( b ) : States that an obligation is discharged to the extent of any payment made by a negotiable instrument unless it is returned or dishonored. 
XXXX XXXX ( b ) ( XXXX ) : Defines lawful money, including postage stamps affixed to negotiable instruments. 
12 U.S. Code 411 : Governs the issuance and receipt of lawful money and its proper application in discharging debts. 
18 U.S. Code 1341 ( Mail Fraud ) : Prohibits the use of mail to execute fraudulent schemes.

18 U.S. Code 1343 ( Wire Fraud ) : Prohibits the use of electronic communication in executing fraud.

Securities Exchange Act of 1934 : Governs securities transactions, including securities fraud. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX Banking XXXX ) : Requires the discharge of debts upon the tender of lawful money. 
Gold Clause : Prohibits the refusal to accept lawful money for the discharge of debts. 
U.S. Constitution : Guarantees the right to contract freely, without interference, including my right to maintain open-ended credit plans. 
Potential Crimes : Theft : CHASE CARD SERVICES has retained my private securities and negotiable instruments without applying them as payments, constituting theft. 
Fraud : Their continued demands for payments after I have satisfied the debt through lawful means indicate fraudulent behavior, possibly in violation of federal fraud statutes. 
Securities Fraud : The mishandling of the securities I tendered suggests that CHASE CARD SERVICES may be engaged in securities fraud under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. 
Language Fraud : CHASE CARD SERVICES has used unclear and deceptive language to obscure my rights, misrepresenting the terms of my agreements, the status of my payments, and the nature of the accounts, which is also deceptive practices. 
Desired Resolution : I request that the CFPB investigate the following : Unlawful retention of securities : Investigate CHASE CARD SERVICES for refusing to process or return the private instruments I tendered as payment. 
Unlawful closure of accounts : Reopen my accounts, as they were unlawfully closed after the debts were discharged. As well as they should reflect an open-ended credit plan at all times. 
Investigation of potential fraud and securities fraud : CHASE CARD SERVICES for potential theft, fraud, language fraud, securities fraud, theft of lawful money. 
Refund overpayments : [ Institution Name ] must refund or credit any overpayments I made when I affixed lawful money ( postage stamps ) to the securities. 
Recognition of my rights as a holder in due course : Ensure that CHASE CARD SERVICES respects my rights as the holder of these securities and negotiable instruments. 
Monetary relief for every violation per day, pursuant to the Federal Reserve Act, U.S.C., C.F.R., and XXXX, that they do not apply my security instruments.

Over the last 6 weeks I have contacted my loan provider on 5-6 separate occasions to inquire about student loan deferment for graduate school enrollment. For background I am a 5th year Biology Ph.D. candidate with the timeline to graduate in XX/XX/XXXX. I came from an extremely low-income background and therefore my parents did not have the credit to co-sign federal student loans. For that reason I had to get private student loans with variable interest rates co-signed with my grandmother to attend XXXX. 

I therefore unfortunately have student loans with Sallie Mae. For the student loans they only allow 48 months of graduate in-school deferment. Therefore this summer I worked throughout the months on XXXX and XXXX to get them to approve a temporary extension of the deferment through XXXX such that I could finish my Ph.D. and not drop out. With the caveat that if I can not get the deferment I would not be able to afford to finish my degree and would have to drop out 8 months before finishing. During this time 3 separate agents told me the deferment would be approved as long as my institution provided the documentation that I was fully enrolled ( they did ). The final agent told me they could see the deferment in my account and to not worry because it had already been applied. From talking the customer advocates today they reiterated that that was in my account for XXXX and XXXX, but was removed in XXXX once the 48 months lapsed. 

I tried to work with them on two more occasions once with a customer service rep and once with a customer advocate to determine any other options to help lower my payments to pay just interest or to get that 8 month extension on my deferment. I was told by both customer service and customer advocates that my only option would be forbearance and I could only use that for 4 of the 8 months I had left in my graduate program. This is because after XXXX I used 8 months of forbearance to do a year of service helping children living in extreme poverty in the XXXX XXXX. 

I also asked if we could refinance them to get a lower or fixed interest rate and they said they do not provide that service, but I could go elsewhere. I am looking into that but that has been difficult because I am still enrolled in school even though the loans I have are from XXXX ( XXXX ). I also disclosed to Sallie Mae that I am also publicly crowd source funding my last year of my Ph.D. due to this circumstance, which is true and has been successful so far. Though unfortunately only successful enough to get me through XXXX not through the rest of the year, so unfortunately I will probably still have to dropout. As a XXXX XXXX XXXX student from a family still living in poverty this is heartbreaking and disgusting. 

My principal on the loan was only ~ {$67000.00} but now I owe more than {$120000.00} due to interest alone and it is disgusting. I am working on my Ph.D. such that I can get the best paying job possible to not only pay off my student loans, but also help my family get out of poverty and have a house of their own one day. I can't pay {$1500.00} a month in student loans as a grad student only makes {$1900.00} a month, but I offered to pay any lesser amount, but they were not willing to work with me it was everything or forbearance or delinquency. 

I also brought up the fact that 3 customer service reps told me on the phone in front of witnesses that my loans would be deferred and not to worry as long as I stayed enrolled in school full-time to then go back on that once XXXX hit. 

I have also been reading a lot about the law suit against XXXXSallie Mae due to forbearance steering of low-income students, and I am heartbroken that my loans were current and not delinquent at the time. Though I wanted to submit this complaint because I would say after speaking to at least 5 agents in XXXX and XXXX of XXXX they have changed none of their practices when it comes to forbearance steering of low-income students and should 100 % be fined or sued again. I am not saying that such that my loan could be forgiven or removed from them, but such that they could not do this ever again. They also gave me an extremely predatory loan and as a low-income student with 0 other options for a student loan for XXXX I had no other option that was it, but that doesn't make it okay. 

Also, they do not offer the interest only graduated repayment option to graduate students because you have to apply for that during the first 18 months after you graduate from XXXX and as graduate students the issue isn't until 48 months after you graduate from XXXX. 

All in all I hope that Sallie Mae gets re-sanctioned because their treatment of me and my student loan in this circumstance has been both inhumane and disgusting. I had said a million times that me finishing my Ph.D. would put me in the best place to pay back the loan without undue financial difficulty, but they just didn't care. To them I am no more than a poor person who was XXXX enough to get a loan with them when I was XXXX to try and better the life of myself and my family.

state: On XX/XX/XXXX, I was approved for {$3500.00} credit with Conn 's. On XX/XX/XXXX, I visited the Conn 's located at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, TX XXXX, ( XXXX ) XXXX to select a bedroom set and grill. During the finalization of the transaction, I was asked to sign the agreement on what appeared to be an XXXX housed in a protective cover. The screen made reading the information obscure, so asked if a copy could be sent to my email. A copy was never sent. I was then told how much I would pay, and I left. The next day, XX/XX/XXXX, I called that Conn 's to cancel the bedroom furniture, but keep the grill. I was told someone would return my call, but after not hearing back from anyone there, I visited the store in person to cancel the bedroom furniture. I asked if I needed to sign anything because of the change and was told no. I was also told that it was not a problem and the grill would be delivered as scheduled. At the time of agreement, I requested that the grill be assembled, which was a {$30.00} fee. The entire purchase was predicated on a 12 month interest free with free delivery agreement, which was advertised throughout the Conn 's showroom. The grill was delivered assembled as scheduled. A month later when I attempted to make my first payment online, I encountered a problem setting up the online account. I contacted the store where I purchased the grill and was told that I had to make the payments at that store 's location. This was difficult because of my work schedule at the time. No one was able to assist me with accessing the account online. When I finally gained access, the website showed that I owed more than XXXX XXXX dollars for the grill. I was finally able to go into the store in XXXX and make the very first payment. When I questioned them about the amount that was displayed on that login, they could not explain. I then asked for a copy of the agreement again, but never received it. I returned to the store in XXXX to make another payment. This is when I learned that the balance for a {$430.00} grill was now almost {$1000.00}. I was also told that it was a loan and not Conn 's credit as I originally thought. I was also told that there was interest and insurance involved that total. I requested to speak with manager after manager, and was told that everything was being done to resolve this issue. Nothing was ever done to help resolve this issue, so in XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a complaint with the XXXX XXXX XXXX siting the same issues I'm siting here. A representative responded that they would change the contract to fix the issue. The contract that was sent showed the same over priced balance. When I pointed this out in a response on the XXXX claim, I was then told that a new contract would be created to resolve the issue. This time, Conn 's waited until after the deadline for my response to move forward or close the matter with them before sending a second contract which didn't change the terms. After that, I received multiple contracts that were back dated and included the same high balance as before. I attempted to XXXX arrangements to settle this account, but they continued to demand that I pay over {$900.00}, even after already paying {$230.00}, which is half of what I actually owed. I never made another payment, and they never attempted to resolve this issue until recently I received mail stating that the balance would be charged off on XX/XX/XXXX if the balance wasn't paid. I called again in hopes of settling the account, but was still being quoted a high amount. On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a complaint the FTC and I informed the rep with whom I had been communicating that I had file this complaint. A XXXX XXXX responded that day. I requested from him to provide me with a copy of charges and fees and the final payoff amount so that I could put this behind me. He responds two days after they charged it off to inform me that it was charged off for less than any of the agreements ever stated. Now I'm receiving several emails a day asking if I wish to settle the account. I believe that Conn 's is purposefully practicing deceptive trade practices, and decided to ignore my attempt to pay the balance in an attempt to further damage my credit with a charge off.

So I called PenFed customer service again ( the 5th, 6th or 7th time, I lost count ). This time I was told to upload ID documents, which I did weeks ago ( carefully preserving the reference numbers given by your software for the upload of each ID ). Still I could not log in to my account. 

Finally, when the seller of the car ( the car for which I obtained the PenFed auto loan that expired because I could not login ) threatened to sue me ( again ) for breach of contract, I contacted you again. 

This time I was told I had not submitted the ID documents, so I gave your customer representative the reference numbers I received from your software at the time I had uploaded the ID documents. 

After asking me to hold, your customer service representative returned to the call, and verified that I had indeed uploaded all the ID documents requested, and that all the ID had been verified, and accepted. 

Then your customer representative told me that the ( real ) problem was that I had conflicting email addresses on my account ( different spellings of what seemed to be the same email address ). After some minutes, he and I figured out that my email address was not transferred correctly by the PenFed software ( copied from one location in your records, to another location in your records ). 

The correct spelling of my email address is : XXXX ( my last name has a space in it, so I use a period to represent the space in XXXX XXXX ). However, your software copied this email address to another location in your records as : XXXX ( ie, without the period following my title, and also without the period that represents the space in my last name ). 

I explained to the customer service representative that the presence of the periods in my email address should not matter, because all email software ignores punctuation marks in email addresses ( ie, XXXX is the same as XXXX ). 

The representative agreed that my it is true that all email software protocols ignore punctuation marks in email addresses, but that the PenFed software does not ignore punctuation in email addresses ( ie, the PenFed software sees XXXX and XXXX as two different addresses ). 

However, ( illogically ), the PenFed software does not transfer any punctuation in email addresses when copying addresses from one location in your records to another location ( in your records ). 


These conflicting software rules alerted your Fraud department that there was a problem with my account. The original customer representatives I spoke with ( in the first months of my account lockout ) were not skilled enough to determine the nature of the problem, so they forwarded the situation to your technical department to solve. 

Evidently, your technical department ( also ) could not figure why I was locked out of my PenFed account, since they never fixed the problem. Perhaps they tried to solve the problem however, they never communicated with me, or with your customer service department. Therefore, your customer service representatives continued to give me an inaccurate answer the many times I called XXXX to say I still could not login ( that the technical department must still be working on the problem ). 

The inaction of the technical department left me hung in the same position for months ( ie, waiting for someone at PenFed to fix the problem, or at least give me an explanation as to why the problem could not be fixed ). 

Instead, my inability to login was always in the hands of your Fraud department. Months have gone by without an explanation ( or with an incorrect explanation ), causing all the damage to me that I described above. 

Your customer representative had the grace to agree with these conclusions, and promised earnestly that he would get the problem corrected by the Fraud department. He assured me that I would be able to login in two more days. 

Well, two days ( and more ) have passed. 

Can you guess what I am going to say next? 
I still can not login! 

Therefore, I am : 1 ) still being sued for breach of contract because I can not purchase the car for which I obtained the now expired auto loan from you, and 2 ) I still can not pay the last two + months bills ( nor pay all the bounced payment charges ) because you reversed the transfers you gave me permission to make ( from my PenFed account to my XXXX account ), and because I could not complete my PenFed personal loan documents ( due to the fact I could not login to my account to do so ). 

So what would like me to do now? 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX, MPH, PhD P.S. I should also say that I am seriously ( perhaps terminally ) ill, XXXX for a decade, almost XXXX XXXX XXXX, and this whole debacle is killing me. 

I expect my login to be activated, and my personal loan and my auto loan applications to be reinstated so that I can pay my bills ( and so that I can sign the acceptance forms on both the personal loan and the auto loan, resolve the breach of contract suit, and pay my all the overdrafts as well as the overdraft charges on my XXXX  account. 

I will certainly be most appreciative of your prompt action in this matter. 

CC : consumerfinance.gov ; www./ncua.gov ; www.dobs.pa.gov In case you need the reference numbers for each piece of ID I uploaded : Identity Authentication - XXXX Government Issued ID Identity Authentication - XXXX Government Issued ID Identity Authentication - XXXX Social Security Card Identity Authentication - XXXX Utility Bill Identity Authentication - XXXX Other ( ID )

I had been a Chase cardholder for over a decade. I have never missed a payment and my account has always been in excellent standing ( as reflected on my credit report ). I tried to purchase some meds that I get by mail order and my payment would not go through. On XX/XX/XXXX I called the customer service line and was informed that my account was closed on XX/XX/XXXX and a letter mailed to me ( which I have still not received to date ). On XXXX and XXXX I made three extra payments, with nothing due at that time. This year I was able to pay off all credit card debt and now pay purchases as they post or at least pay off the card in full every cycle. I did not realize that Chases online system auto-populates the payment funding account to the last account you used so the payments tried to pull from savings that I dont often use. As soon as I realized what happened ( before even receiving notices ) I paid the card from my checking account with I had originally intended. 
Chase has used the returned payments as a reason to close my credit card. There was no warning or communication that these returns could cause negative account consequences. The returned item notices gave no indication of closure and even thanked me for my business. They also did not charge me any, so it seems that it was not even serious enough to warrant a fee. Clearly, the decision to close my account was not made at the time of the returns but almost two months later. The timing is suspicious. I had an {$18000.00} credit line which closing could affect my credit score. The only reason I can see that they would review my account and close it almost two months later is that they are using it as an  excuse to close my account because I dont carry a balance ( they dont make interest off of me ) and I redeem about $ XXXX {$60.00} of points in statement credits per month ( which there is nothing against in the account agreement and the whole reason I opened this card ). The reason provided to me over the phone on XX/XX/XXXX by XXXX a supervisor ( who refused to let me speak with anyone higher ) was that my account was closed because of the returned payments. However, according to my account agreement, there is no clause that states returned payments could result in account closure. The only clause that deals with returns state We may charge this fee if the payment you offer to us is not honored, is returned unpaid, or can not be processed which has nothing about closing an account ( and was not charged ). The only other clause  that allows them to close an account is We are not obligated to honor every transaction, and we may close or suspend your account. Sometimes we close accounts based not on your actions or inactions, but on our business needs. however the reason given to me was based on my action and not a business need. It is clear in their agreement that my contract/account was not terminated in a legally allowable manner ( see attached account agreement ). 
I called on XX/XX/XXXX and requested to speak with a manager. I was  transferred to XXXX a supervisor who kept telling me what dont you understand, you had a returned payment. XXXX stated they dont have an external email so could not send me my account agreement, he told me it is not available online, and they could also not send me it via the online messaging system. He also would not cite to me the clause that gives them the right to close it. Seemingly he did not want me to look at it. Also, he stated that a loan is not a contract, which is grossly incorrect. On XXXX I messaged chase that I had a right to obtain my account agreement to which they sent me a direct online link. Why was this not supplied immediately the first time I called on XX/XX/XXXX. 
This closure appears to be a deceptive way to get out of their relationship with me since they dont see my account as profitable, with complete disregard for their effect on my credit and overall financial health. I also have all my automatic I have to switch, not to mention the fees I would have incurred from other companies if those payments bounce since I did not receive any notice it was closed. They say they sent me a closure letter the same day the account was closed XX/XX/XXXX, but then why does it not show up in the Notice and Letters section of online banking ( See screenshots attached ) like the returned payments notices do, which suggests a closure notice was not actually sent. To date, I have not received any closure notice. This to me appears to be a violation of Reg Z closure notice requirements, a breach of contract/account agreement, and the whole issue is a possible UDAAP violation. 

I have worked in the financial sector for over a decade and we would not dream of closing someones account who 1 ) for a reason not legally supported by the account agreement, 2 ) when the client had over a decade of excellent account history, and posed no threat to the financial institution, 3 ) for one mistake, that was an extra payment, 4 ) that did not negatively impact our financial institution, and 5 ) that was the fault of the online system auto-populating the  wrong payment account. Their actions are unconscionable and I am being retaliated against for not being a profitable client who is financial responsibility and does not regularly pay interest anymore.

Re : Request for Removal of Inaccurate Credit Reporting Account Numbers : XXXX & XXXX To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to formally dispute and request the immediate removal of inaccurate information being reported to the credit bureaus regarding my private loan accounts, referenced above. Despite my efforts to resolve these issues, I have discovered that Sallie Mae continues to report negative and misleading information related to these loans. 

Loan Account # XXXX : Original Balance : {$20000.00} Settled Amount : {$10000.00}, paid in full to XXXX  XXXX  ( collection agency ). 
Taxable Settlement : I paid taxes on the settlement amount as required by law. 
Loan Account # XXXX : Original Balance : {$4000.00} Settled Amount : {$1500.00}, paid in full to XXXX  XXXX  ( collection agency ). 
Taxable Settlement : I also paid taxes on this settlement amount. 
I was under the understanding that these loans were settled in full with the collection agency, XXXX XXXX, and that Sallie Mae would no longer be involved in reporting these accounts. However, despite the full settlement and the fact that I have complied with all necessary steps ( including paying taxes on the settlement amounts ), Sallie Mae continues to inaccurately report a balance due and/or negative information related to these loans. 

This ongoing mismanagement is causing harm to my credit profile and financial well-being. I am requesting that Sallie Mae immediately : Correct the inaccurate information being reported to all three major credit bureaus ( XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX ) to reflect that these accounts were settled in full with XXXX XXXX. 
Delete any erroneous balances or derogatory marks that are currently affecting my credit history. 
Provide written confirmation to me that these corrections have been made and that all information has been updated accordingly with the credit bureaus. 
Please be aware that under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), I am entitled to have accurate and up-to-date information reflected in my credit reports. I trust that Sallie Mae will take the necessary steps to rectify this situation promptly and avoid further damage to my credit. 

Should you need any documentation to support my claim, including settlement agreements, tax records, or correspondence with XXXX XXXX, please do not hesitate to contact me at the above address or phone number. 

FCRA Violations by Sallie Mae The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) is designed to ensure that consumers credit reports are accurate, fair, and private. It also holds credit reporting agencies ( and data furnishers like Sallie Mae ) accountable for providing accurate information. In this case, it appears that Sallie Mae has potentially violated several sections of the FCRA : Section 1681s-2 ( a ) : Duty of Furnishers of Information to Provide Accurate Information Under this section, creditors ( like Sallie Mae ) are required to provide accurate information to the credit reporting agencies. If they are aware that the information being reported is inaccurate, they must correct it. Given that you settled your loans with XXXX XXXX and the debt was paid, Sallie Mae is obligated to report this accurately. Reporting incorrect balance information or an unresolved debt after a settlement is a violation of this provision. 

Section 1681i : Procedure in Case of Disputed Information This section gives consumers the right to dispute inaccurate information on their credit reports. Once a dispute is filed, the credit reporting agencies are required to investigate and resolve the dispute within a reasonable timeframe, typically 30 days. If you have already disputed the inaccurate information, and it has not been corrected, Sallie Mae may be in violation of this provision by failing to investigate and correct the inaccuracies.

Section 1681e ( b ) : Accuracy of Information Under this section, the FCRA mandates that credit reports must be accurate and not misleading. If Sallie Mae is continuing to report a balance after the loan was settled, they are violating the FCRAs requirement that information must be accurate and not misleading.

Section 1681s-2 ( b ) : Duty to Investigate Disputes If a dispute is raised by the consumer, the furnisher ( Sallie Mae ) is required to investigate the issue with the credit reporting agencies. If youve already raised this issue directly with Sallie Mae and they have not investigated or corrected the errors, they would be violating this provision. 

I look forward to your prompt resolution of this matter.

state: I received a check from XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/2022 in the amount of {$1400.00} and deposited it into my checking account with Chase through Mobile Deposit on XX/XX/2022. Friday XX/XX/XXXX the funds from the mobile deposit were released to my account and no longer showed pending. Then Thursday XX/XX/XXXX all funds were shown to have been removed from my checking account and my account was completely closed. I called Chase customer Service twice, once on XX/XX/2022 then again XX/XX/2022 both times I was informed that the check could not be verified by the maker because no number for XXXX XXXX was in Chases Database. I then went into The XXXX TX Chase branch and spoke to someone and was informed the same information and was told to reach out to XXXX XXXX and get a phone number from them that Chase could call to verify the check. From there I went to XXXX XXXX in person and spoke to the cashiers office and was informed that the funds were released to Chase and then I was given the number to the head of the Cashiers office and the Vice President for obtaining verification. I again went up to Chase and informed an advisor of the issue and provided him with the number to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and Cashiers office. I was then told that the phone numbers were not in the database and that they would not be able to call anyone to verify the check and the funds can not be released until Chase has verified the check with the maker. I then asked if verification could be made with XXXX since that is who XXXX XXXX banks with and was told that was not possible. From there I asked what I could do to obtain the {$1400.00} and was informed that the branch was going to submit a complaint to Chase and wait for a response. I was denied a copy of any of the transactions and was never given an alert to the account being put on hold or closed. There was no answer when I requested a timeline of when the situation would be resolved and was told there was no way to ensure me that it ever would be.

There is an illegal, fraudulent and willfully oppressive sale of property scheduled for my home at XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX California on XX/XX/XXXX. Bayview Loan Servicing lacks the contractual authority under the Deed of Trust and the statutory authority under Civil Code 2924 to conduct a nonjudicial foreclosure sale. 

Bayview is obligated not to foreclose absent certain conditions precedent as stated in Section 22 of the Deed of Trust and Bayview breached that obligation by initiating a foreclosure sale although the conditions precedent were absent. The alleged default exists only by virtue of misconduct on the part of Bayview and XXXX XXXX XXXX and their own breach of its terms. ( See Civ. Code, 1511, ( 1 ) [ performance excused when such performance is prevented or delayed by the act of the creditor ]. ) Their actions do not conform sufficiently with the DOT as to allow Bayview to invoke the power of sale. 

Under California contract law, " hindrance of the other party 's performance operates to excuse that party 's nonperformance. '' ( Erich v. Granoff ( 1980 ) 109 Cal.App.3d 920, 93 ; " A foreclosure sale in which performance has been prevented could be considered illegal and even willfully oppressive, Citrus El Dorado , LLC v. Stearns Bank NA , No. E067610 ( Cal. Ct. App. Apr. 11, 2019 ). This supported an action for wrongful foreclosure. 

An obligor may not prevent the performance of an obligee and then demand a tender of performance that the obligor itself frustrated. See Cal. Civ. Code 1511-12 ; Harris v. Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., Case No. 12-cv-05629-JST ( N.D. Cal. Apr. 30, 2013 ) ; " By force of the provisions of section 1511 of the Civil Code, prevention by one party will excuse want of performance or delay on the part of the other. '' ( 6 Cal.Jur., p. 436, sec . 261. ) 1 " A party to a contract can not take advantage of his own act or omission to  escape liability therefrom, and performance of a contract is excused when prevented by the acts of the opposite party, or is rendered impossible by him. '' ( Ray Thomas, Inc., v. Cowan, 99 Cal.App. 140 [ 277 P. 1086 ]. ) Taylor v. Sapritch, 38 Cal. App. 2d 478, 101 P.2d 539 ( Ct. App. 1940. ) The sale is fraudulent as the " default '' was induced by XXXX 's as part of a scheme to increase profitability at the homeowner 's expense by offering improved loan terms if payments were skipped then refusing payments and initiating foreclosure. The homeowner is kept in default as long as possible while they earn special servicing fees and allow payments to accrue at the note rate. Bayview can then either modify and add the arrears to the principal and earn interest on interest. Or they may choose to foreclose despite having induced default and being themselves the party in breach. 

This is only the latest in the systematic pattern of unlawful conduct that began with a predatory loan that was procedurally and substantively unconscionable with deception at origination and monthly payments in excess of my income. As a result, I ended up in Chapter XXXX where the payments were 89 % of my income not including overcharged escrow. 

Throughout the life of the loan XXXX and Bayview have exploited their position of authority and control by deceptive and fraudulent means in an effort to benefit at my expense.This is a willfully oppressive abuse of power. 

The disparity of economics requires a homeowner to either accept the loss of their home or divert funds that could have made loan payments into a Quixotic effort in the legal system against an opponent with comparatively limitless resources. 

It is outrageous for financial institutions to deliberately harm consumers for profit. It is foreseeable that homeowners subjected to these practices, having their homes wrongfully taken from then will experience extreme emotional distress. Prolonged states of XXXX XXXX, it is well known, can lead to physical ailments. After years of fighting for my home I've suffered a XXXX related XXXX injury that impedes my XXXX XXXX XXXX and appears to be a XXXX condition. Mobility seems a high price but one I've been willing to pay to keep my home. If the sale goes through I'll have neither.

XX/XX/XXXX To whom it may concern, In XXXX of XXXX, my spouse ( deceased on XX/XX/XXXX ) received a letter from Wells Fargo informing him that he had been turned down for a {$5000.00} Line of Credit. This application was apparently then backdated and added me as the primary borrower with him listed as secondary. That application was subsequently approved. I have/had no knowledge of participating in this process and did not attend any closing or other meeting on this issue. I also found a notation in his writing on one letter authorizing auto-deduction from my personal checking account. 
Following my husbands death in XX/XX/XXXX, I had to take over handling bill payment for the first time and to begin work on identifying accounts that I had no previous knowledge of. It took me a little time to gather what information I could and to pursue gaining closure on those accounts. I contacted Wells Fargo in XXXX of XXXX asking how I became listed on this Line of Credit account and also who had authorized auto-deduction from my personal checking account. I was told that I was listed as the primary borrower and that my spouse had authorized auto deductions. I explained at that time that I had no knowledge of the account and that I had not approved it. I was informed that since I was primary, it was my responsibility. They did agree to discontinue auto deductions and to begin billing me. 
I was referred to a different customer service department to further explore the account information. A Mr. XXXX XXXX was the assigned representative. I asked to have a copy of the application signature page sent to me so that I could verify my signature. I also asked how it was possible that a Line of Credit for {$5000.00} now had a ceiling of {$15000.00}. No information was offered. XXXX XXXX informed me that they had no copy of the application signature page available, nor proof that I was in the office, but that since I was listed as primary the debt was my responsibility. He further stated that the fact transfers had been made and payments had been made that also indicated it was my responsibility. I told him that of course I had made payments as I didnt want my credit impacted while attempting to sort this out. I asked him to look at the records because there was never any transfer made to my account and provided him with the number. It took several weeks to get this information which was of no significance. He refused to speak with me further, saying he had explained all he was going to. I spoke with an attorney to ask how to proceed with the lack of information and the poor communication. She contacted the department on my behalf, was given a new case number and a representative named XXXX on XXXX. She advised me to give this person a call to introduce myself and to see what further information could be provided. I did so. XXXX was pleasant and told me that it could take up to 10 business days to get the information and to get back to me. When she did contact me on XX/XX/XXXX, the information was basically the same : They had not located the signature page but there was a letter mailed from the branch. She maintained that there was enough research to say that both my husband and I were responsible. I was then referred to the hardship department. 
I passed this information via summary to my attorney and asked what next steps I should take. She recommended that I get in touch with the hardship department and inform them that since apparently the bank can not provide : 1. That I applied for or signed for the loan, either in person or on paper 2. That I ever requested the loan increase 3. That I personally ever received any funds from this account 4.  That I ever authorized auto payments from my personal account I should ask the hardship department to confirm in writing that my name would be removed from the loan. 

I contacted XXXX on the hardship team and he referred me to an XXXX on the hardship team. I conveyed the above information as stated. He informed me that I needed to speak with the Executive Team regarding the situation and connected me by conference call to XXXX on that team. I spoke with XXXX for a few minutes and reiterated the entire experience, and he nicely let me know that I had been connected to the right people as the Executive Team was the only level that would be authorized to make changes as they were the final level of investigation. He then gave me the name of a XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, along with her direct dial number and yet another case number. On XX/XX/XXXX I was told that XXXX XXXX would contact me within 10 business days. I heard nothing from her, so on XX/XX/XXXX, I called and had to leave a message as she was out until XX/XX/XXXX. Again, I heard nothing so I called on XX/XX/XXXX and again left a message. 

When I had a conversation with XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, she informed me that per the letter she had sent, a Wells Fargo Card and a NOTR had been used as my ID. I told her that was interesting as Id never had a Wells Fargo Credit Card, she quickly said well it could have been a debit card. I then asked her what a NOTR was, since I had no idea. She told me she didnt know what that was. On the form that was included with the letter ( received the same day as the phone call ), it said no drivers license was provided. Again, I asked her how that could be since I use my drivers license as my ID all the time, and would never be without it. She couldnt answer that either, but said that the form didnt allow her to add any information (? ). Her bottom line was that theres nothing they can do because the evidence points to me being responsible. Again, what evidence? 

She advised me to speak with the Hardship Team to discuss lowering the monthly payment. I did place a call to them but it was never returned. 

I dont believe this account is my responsibility. I have absolutely no recollection of any meeting or closing appointment. They can not offer any signature proof or any proof that I was ever in the office for this application. They can not or chose not to explain how a {$5000.00} credit limit was raised to a {$15000.00} limit while my deceased spouse was handling financial arrangements. They can not demonstrate that I benefited in any way from this account by virtue of the fact there is no record of any transfer or cash advancement ever made to my personal checking account. You will also note that on the form provided by XXXX XXXX, my spouse is shown as employed at the time when in reality he had been retired for several years. Nothing about this situation is accurate or my responsibility.

PayPal wont automatically switch between the two rates based on transaction size, so if you opt for the micropayments plan, you really need to make sure its the best option based on your individual processing history. Generally speaking, if you sell digital goods online ( single songs or digital albums, or other low-value items ), this is the plan you should look for. 
In addition, qualified 501 ( c ) ( 3 ) organizations who go through the verification process are eligible for a discount for online transactions : Nonprofit Discount Rate : 2.2 % +  {$0.00} Sadly, PayPal doesnt offer a discounted rate for in-person transactions processed through its mPOS or a partner POS system, so the discounted rate would apply only to online sales or donations. However, keep in mind that some software providers also offer nonprofit discounts, so if youve integrated PayPal with accounting software, a POS app, or another third party, you should also check whether that company offers a discount. 
PayPal Monthly Fees Remember, there are two options for accepting PayPal on your site that charge nothing beyond transaction fees : PayPal Checkout and PayPal Payments Standard. Both allow you to accept payments on your website but will redirect to the PayPal site to complete the transaction. If you prefer to keep customers on your own page, or if youd like a virtual terminal to take payments over the phone, youll need PayPal Payments Pro : Paypal Payments Pro : {$30.00} per month The biggest advantage, as I said, is that the Pro account lets you keep customers on your page to finish the checkout process. You can completely design your own checkout page. In addition, Pro subscribers get access to the Virtual Terminal to accept payments by phone, mail, and fax. 
Unfortunately, PayPal Payments Pro doesnt include an option for Recurring Billing. Subscription services are hugely popular and if you want to offer them with PayPal, that will run you an extra {$10.00} per month on top of the Pro plan. If you dig a little deeper, youll also see that PayPal offers free recurring billing for users who have implemented PayPal Express Checkout, but not PayPal Standard. 
Finally, its worth noting that PayPal offers its own gateway, the PayFlow gateway, to process payments. It has a high degree of compatibility, so it works with most payment processors. So if you want to sell online but dont want to use PayPal as your primary payment processor, and your chosen processor doesnt offer a gateway, this could be an option. PayFlow supports two plans : PayFlow Link : This pay-as-you-go option costs {$0.00} per transaction, and PayPal charges nothing for setup or monthly fees. Using Link, you can embed a checkout form on your website that will redirect to the PayPal site to complete the transaction. Link also adds PayPal and PayPal Credit buttons. 
Payflow Pro : At $ XXXX/month for the Pro Plan, theres no questioning the value. You wont pay setup fees or per-transaction fees. PayPal doesnt even put a limit on the volume. With the Pro option, you get a completely customizable checkout page thats hosted on your own website, with the options to add PayPal and PayPal Credit options. 
As I said, PayPal really has something for everyone. I dont know that I can say it has everything everyone would need, but itll definitely tick most of the boxes for most people. While PayPal still is dominating the online space, it definitely has moved beyond to encompass multiple sales channels. Being able to manage in-person and online sales from a single platform is a major point of convenience.

2. Potential Illegality of Balloon Payment : I have become aware that the " voluntary payment '' clause in the Agreement may constitute a balloon payment arrangement. This type of payment structure is governed by specific regulations under California statutory and case law. However, the contractual terms do not expressly refer to this as a balloon payment or provide the necessary disclosures as required by law. utory and case law supporting the legality of the clause.

I expect a prompt response within a reasonable timeframe from the date of receipt of this letter. Failure to address these issues satisfactorily may result in further legal action to protect my rights as a consumer under the laws of California.

I made an online purchase on XX/XX/XXXX of {$78.00} and paid through paypal. The next day, I saw that I was billed twice, and another XXXX payments had been authorized. I immediately contacted paypal and alerted them of the fraud. After checking my browser, I saw that at the time I made the purchase, paypal checkout was accessed multiple times. And I saw that I was never sent the purchase confirmation from the seller. Paypal claimed that it was me that authorized the second payment and additional XXXX future payments, and denied my claim. 

I appealed, and collected lots of documentation, including the screenshot of the item, a screenshot of my browser history showing XXXX checkouts in just a couple minutes. 

Paypal contacted the 'seller ' who sent them a tracking number, and again my claim was denied. I contacted to postal service, who sent me a picture of the package with the tracking number very clear. It was addressed to someone else- not my name- and another address, and showed the weight of the package was XXXXXXXX XXXX The only thing in common was that the package was addressed to someone in my zipcode. Apparently, for paypal, anything shipped to anywhere and anyone in my zipcode was enough proof that I received the item. Even the shipper on the package label was not the same as the seller. 

The item I purchased was XXXXXXXX XXXX. I again supplied paypal with the info the post office supplied, and provided the description of the item purchased showing the XXXXXXXX XXXX weight of the package they claimed was shipped to me, and showing them that the XXXX items I was charged for ( charged twice for XXXX order ) had the same tracking number for each 'order '. I even supplied proof of the postal weight limit from the local postmaster. 

The attempted purchase was XX/XX/XXXX at XXXXXXXX XXXX. At XXXXXXXX XXXX the same date, the company authorized additional payment to be charged to my account. At XXXXXXXX XXXX, on XX/XX/XXXX, the second payment was charged to my account. with XXXX more payments to be taken. 

It was about XXXX XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX when I discovered all this and immediately reported it to paypal. Paypal denied my first claim just XXXX minutes after I submitted it, saying that I authorized the payments. 

I spent the next several days going back and forth, and I had to battle each charge separately and file everything twice, as paypal considered it as XXXX separate purchases. 

I got the tracking info from the post office on XX/XX/XXXX, including an email from the local postmaster, and a pic of the package, and submitted it immediately to paypal. 

Paypal informed me that they would review the info and issue a decision is just a few days. later extended to XX/XX/XXXX, and said they would give the seller a chance to submit info. The website I bought from is still active, but the website that billed me is no longer active, so the scammers likely switched to another account. Paypal hasn't replied to my requests that they refund the money. 

And now I have learned that paypal does this regularly, as part of their business model, and instead of honoring their money back protection guarantee, they force consumers to go into small claims court to receice money back. I'm XXXX XXXX XXXX, in poor health, unable to walk long distances, and because they have added a prohibition against class actions, and insist on either arbitration or small claims court to acheive satisfaction, there consumer protections are essentially a fraud. It will be an excessive burden for me, and likely most consumers. They profit from every transaction, and don't want to return even the {$150.00} total they have charged me. They also told me that the charges would be removed until this was settled, but the charges remain. 

Since paypal profitted, they are actually aiding and abetting the criminals by letting the seller submit fake tracking info, and having paypal willfully, knowlingly accept it without checking. They forced XXXX to spend hours trying to get the info from the post office. Paypal is detrimentally relying on the fact that the post office doesn't generally give out tracking info to anyone but the adressee.But I was able to show the postmaster that paypal had me listed as the recipient, so showed that fraud was occurring

state: On XX/XX/2019, I applied for a home mortgage loan. The loan officer suggested several items that needed to be cleared from my credit. I contacted debt collector Rent Recovery ( Original debt is XXXX XXXX ) on XX/XX/2019. I spoke to a representative to inquire about a settlement to get this off the credit bureaus. They gave me 2 solutions. They proceeded to go over charges the debt is a total of {$7800.00}. A previous water bill was included in this amount. I stated that I previously filled that amount in bankruptcy, but my bankruptcy was dismissed. The representative said she will have to talk this over with her manager and to call her the next morning. When I called the next morning, I was told my file was in current bankruptcy status, and to contact my lawyer and they hung up the phone. I called back, proceeded to give my name, and was told again, Mam your in bankruptcy status, and Im going to have to disconnect the call. I called back again, this time I didnt give my name, but asked to speak to a manager, because I was not in bankruptcy status. They switched me over, and then that person said they would have to disconnect the call. I called back, to ask, can I please have an email, or other contact information where I can show Im not in bankruptcy status. A representative told me to mail in a letter from the law office that says my bankruptcy was dismissed. I asked can an email it or fax. The representative said they didnt have an email or fax number, they gave me the address. I went to XXXX  on XX/XX/2019 ( please see attachment ). I sent a letter saying my bankruptcy was dismissed. It was received on XX/XX/2019. I called Rent Recovery on XX/XX/2019, and asked them if they received the letter, a rep said Mam you are in bankruptcy status, please have your lawyer contact us. On XXXX XXXX, I went to work late to go up to the bankruptcy office. I told them my situation, I also called in to a representative from the bankruptcy office, and a representative from the bankruptcy office called on 3 way to Rent Recovery to explain that I was not in any active bankruptcy. The representative from Rent Recovery told the representative from XXXX XXXX  office, Mam she has to wait unit her file is uploaded, Im going to disconnect now. I then reached out to the original creditor on Social Media and called them ( Please see attachment ). Still at attempts to speak to someone about this account I wasnt getting anywhere, next, I called to put in a dispute with the 2 credit bureau XXXX  and XXXX. After reviewing my credit report from XXXX, Rent Recovery first appeared on this report on XX/XX/2019. Then it was removed XXXX  XXXX, its no longer there. However, It appeared on XXXX  report on XX/XX/2019, and its still there. I called to file a dispute and A representative from XXXX  says its not listed in bankruptcy status, I said I know but they refuse to talk to me. XXXX  and XXXX  are investigating my dispute. On XX/XX/XXXX I received an email from XXXX XXXX, saying they reached out to Rent Recovery, and they emailed my bankruptcy dismissal letter. And a representative from Rent Recovery said they will be in contact with me by Monday. I asked, if they gave the letter, they spoke to bankruptcy tepstentatives why wouldnt they just update my file today. I then called Rent Recovery again, and they said my file was still in bankruptcy status. This company is deliberately trying to keep derogatory information on my file.

Dear CFPB, I am writing to file a complaint against OneMain Financial regarding their use of high-pressure sales tactics and potentially misleading information about application deadlines for a title loan. I believe these practices may violate CFPB rules and regulations, particularly those related to Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) and the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). 
Details of the Incident : I recently applied for a title loan through OneMain Financial, which resulted in a hard credit pull. 
Following my application, I received an excessive number of phone calls- 5 calls within 3 days. 
During my interactions with their representative, I experienced several concerning practices : a. The representative used high-pressure sales tactics to rush my decision-making process. 
b. When I expressed needing more time to consider the loan, the representative provided ambiguous or potentially misleading information about application deadlines. 
c. The representative implied various arbitrary deadlines ( Friday, then Monday, then Wednesday ) for submitting my information, creating a false sense of urgency. 
d. Only after I voiced concerns about these tactics did the representative disclose that the actual deadline was 26 days from the start of the application. 
When confronted about these tactics, the representative denied using them, stating she never explicitly mentioned the earlier deadlines, despite heavily implying them during our conversation. 

Potential Violations : Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) : The creation of artificial deadlines and false urgency could be considered deceptive, as it misled me about the true nature of the offer and the time available to make a decision. 


Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) : The high-pressure tactics used may have been an attempt to rush me through the disclosure process or obscure important information, potentially violating TILA regulations.

Request for Action : I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate OneMain Financial 's sales practices, particularly regarding : The use of high-pressure sales tactics. 
The creation of artificial deadlines and false sense of urgency. 
The clarity and accuracy of information provided about application deadlines and processes. 

I believe these practices not only affected my experience but may be impacting other consumers as well. I ask that appropriate penalties be applied if violations are found, and that OneMain Financial be required to revise their sales practices to comply with CFPB regulations. 
Thank you for your attention to this matter. I am willing to provide any additional information if needed.

To Whom It May Concern : We are writing this complaint out of shear frustration after dealing with an already stressful year in 2020 being adversely impacted by the coronavirus financially, CMG Financial has been haphazard in their handling of our mortgage as the servicer. Specifically, I would like to highlight their inability to share information with accuracy and communicating in an expeditious and factual manner that enables the mortgagee to make informed decisions. Please see the timeline of events below : XX/XX/XXXX Contacted CMG to enroll in the COVID-19 Mortgage Forbearance Program due to significantly reduced income as a result of the pandemic. Over the phone we were advised that we could enroll without any paperwork over the phone for a period of 12 months with the option to put the years payments on the back of the loan with a partial claim. 

XXXX XXXX With this assurance we were able to breathe a bit and checked back in to confirm if there was anything needed of us in preparation with the year ending in Q3/Q4. It was our plan to avoid any surprises and plan ahead since this was unchartered territory. A representative advised us that we would automatically be eligible for the partial claim option as it is on the Servicer to comply with FHA in what is offered to the mortgagee. 

XX/XX/XXXX XXXX auto and homeowners insurance from XXXX to XXXX, due to better rates. Provided XXXX with mailing address for CMG in order to facilitate payment of annual homeowners premium. 

XX/XX/XXXX Called CMG to confirm expiration of existing forbearance and was advised we needed to complete the loan modification to be considered for the partial claim and nothing else was available to extend the forbearance even with the new pending legislation under the new Biden Administration. Therefore we proceeded accordingly with completing the loan modification package. 

XX/XX/XXXX Learned from a third party, XXXX XXXX XXXX that our homeowners policy expired on Friday, XX/XX/XXXX due to none payment of the policy premium. We immediately contacted CMG and XXXX for clarity. XXXX indicated they sent correspondence to CMG in XXXX and throughout Q1 XXXX to avoid a lapse and never received any response back. CMG indicated they never received any information at the XXXX XXXX address which is what was provided in XX/XX/XXXX to the mortgagee. At this time, the CMG representative provided me with an email address to send the new homeowners policy ( as though it would be easy to get new insurance given the lapse and having a recent claim on file ). It was extremely troubling having learned we were without homeowners insurance following the extreme freeze which had recently occurred in the XXXX area. 

There were subsequent calls to CMG to share our disdain and disappointment for placing us in this position. XXXX with CMG, ID # XXXX handled the bulk of the call, took notes and called back to advise us there was nothing to be done to recover the expired homeowners policy with XXXX. 

Our quest began to shop for homeowners insurance, now with two negatives : Lapsed coverage, Potential increased/higher premium, and Current/recent homeowners claim In desperation we were only able to obtain a policy which nearly doubled our annual premium with our last insurer from {$1600.00} to {$3300.00} with XXXX XXXX. There were several nos before we got this latest coverage. In fear this policy would also lapse from non-payment by CMG, I made sure to email XXXX as advised from my last call with a CMG representative on XX/XX/XXXX. Confirmation was received on XX/XX/XXXX via email that the new policy information had been received and would be processed. 

As a follow-up measure, I contacted CMG once more on XX/XX/XXXX to see what the status was on processing the new policy premium with XXXX Insurance. Upon calling, I was advised to submit the bill for the new policy to a third-party website as a surefire way that payment would be prompt. I was puzzled since I was under the impression the email and confirmation would be sufficient. As advised, I uploaded the documentation as requested to this new site. It is the inconsistencies with information that is shared with mortgagees that contributes to the continued frustration with CMG.

On a separate issue surrounding the COVID-19 Mortgage Forbearance Program, we called on XX/XX/XXXX and was advised at this time that CMG was now offering the option to extend our existing forbearance an additional 6-months which would total the allowed 18-months and expire on XX/XX/XXXX at which time the first mortgage payment would be due. The CMG representative indicated this option only opened up as of XX/XX/XXXX. Since our financial situation hadnt yet improved we requested for the CMG representative to proceed with this setup over the phone and to disregard the loan modification process which was recently initiated. 

On XX/XX/XXXX we inquired on another issue regarding the handling of the shortage on the account but continued to be routed to the loss mitigation group. While in this maze of calls, we inquired about the status of the 6-month extension for the existing forbearance. At this time, we learned that in fact the additional 6-months hadnt been added as confirmed earlier that month. In fact, the CMG representative indicated that the 6-month forbearance could not be added until the loan modification was cleared/removed from the account. We were under the impression that these things had been addressed in their systems internally. Following a lengthy phone call and extended wait times, we were assured that all had been updated as the other CMG representative was not correct in how the forbearance was entered on XX/XX/XXXX. 

On the morning of XX/XX/XXXX in the 9 oclock hour we contacted CMG once again to gain more clarity as to what exactly was taking place with our mortgage account. After speaking with XXXX XXXX for over an hour in a half, we further learned the following : Mortgagees are not allowed a term of an additional 6-months forbearance, only 3 months ; Again it appears the additional extended forbearance was still not placed correctly on the mortgage account ; It was no guarantee that we would be eligible for the partial claim since their records showed we were 13 months outstanding and it was up to underwriting to review ; and We needed to check back on XX/XX/XXXX to be sure the disaster template was updated on the mortgage account by loss mitigation to the COVID-19 Mortgage Forbearance Program With an anxious feeling we had been given the run around with CMG and the level of incompetence with the many representatives and inconsistencies with the information provided, we requested to have a supervisor call us. As of the writing of this complaint the supposed request which is standard 24-48 hours timeframe to hear back from a supervisor has yet to happen.

Our next steps for reprisal and accuracy of the information provided to us as FHA mortgagees prompted a call to FHA. On the two occasions we called, XXXX XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, FHA advised us differently than what CMG advised. Attached are the concerns which were raised and the information from FHA. We have no other choice at this point but to seek help in ensuring our home is secure and sound as our primary residence following the end of the COVID-19 Forbearance Mortgage Program.
