I, XXXX XXXX, applied online to a group of companies offering personal loans. 

I was under the impression that I was dealing with companies registered in the United States in a particular state ( Montana in this case ). It is believed that Bright Lending is charging approximately 685 % annual interest on a {$300.00} dollar loan with weekly installments of {$40.00} dollars. Three payments have been made with approximately 5 principal payments made between installment dates. Approximately {$150.00} to {$160.00} dollars up to this point has been made. Bright Lending is refusing to apply the additional payments towards principal payments. After further investigation, Bright Lending is believed to be breaking the law by charging annual rates above the State of Montana and the District of Columbia 's " Cap Interest Rates. '' The State of Montana does not have Bright Lending or any of it's affiliates listed as registered businesses. 

Bright Lending is believed to be working from an " off-shore haven '' ( XXXX ) where the site is listed as being hosted via a XXXX Search. Additionally a traceroute of the IP address indicates off-shore computer servers. 

My goals were to pay off the loan as quickly as possible within the District of Columbia 's Cap Rate of 24 %. It is believed that Bright Lending is a bogus site being operated by some third party refusing to be registered as a corporation in the US. 

It is believed that my phones were rerouted by Bright Lending in order to put me in a compromising situation relative to the loan.

I purchased an XXXX in XXXX with a loan from HSBC BANK XXXX XXXX Sometime in XXXX or XXXX, I paid off the loan and placed the ATV on non-op with the XXXX DMV. Recently I have fixed the XXXX  and went to register it to find that I still have a lien on the title from HSBC BANK XXXX XXXX. The DMV  said that I will need a lien release from HSBC BANK XXXX XXXX. Below is a summary of the times I reached out to HSBC USA ( took over HSBC BANK XXXX XXXX ) and the outcomes. 

XX/XX/XXXX : Called HSBC USA and was given an email address ( XXXX ) to send details regarding my request. I sent a .jpg image of the vehicle registration to the email address and asked for them to look into the title / lien release. I was told I should have a response within 4 to 5 days. 

XX/XX/XXXX : Follow up email sent asking for an update. 

XX/XX/XXXX : Called HSBC again to follow up and was given a timeframe for response of 7 to 10 days, which has elapsed as well. 

XX/XX/XXXX : First response from XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) saying they could not open the attachment and to send them : Registered owners name, Year, Make and model, VIN and Requestor name and Mailing address to send the lien release to. I responded with all the requested information that day. 

XX/XX/XXXX : Email from XXXX ( no person named ) asking for Registered owners name, Year, Make and model, VIN and Requestor name and Mailing address to send the lien release to ( again ). The reply had the original picture of the registration in the body of the email, which has all of the requested information as well. I replied back that day saying this is the 3rd time I am now sending them the information but again, give them all of the details they are requesting. 

XX/XX/XXXX : Email from XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ) asking for Registered owners name, Year, Make and model, VIN and Requestor name and Mailing address to send the lien release to ( again ). I reply that day stating this is now the 4th time sending the information but yet again, send the details in the body of the email. I get a response from XXXX XXXX XXXX stating : " We are sorting all No interest letter request from XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/XXXX. If you send multiple request during this period. Youll be receiving responses for all the emails you send especially if details provided are not complete. '' This email showed all of the details I had sent them early in the day with all of the information they were requesting ( Registered owners name, Year, Make and model, VIN and Requestor name and Mailing address ). I replied with " I am not sure what that all means but can you now confirm you have all of the details you need? As I mentioned, I have sent all of the information 4 times now. I did not reach out till XX/XX/XXXX originally with this information, then again on XX/XX/XXXX, followed by the same request on XX/XX/XXXX and yet again this morning. '' XX/XX/XXXX : I called HSBC USA to follow up on this matter. I was on the phone with them for an hour and ended up talking to a virtual assistant in another country who was chatting with XXXX XXXX XXXX about all of the emails she or no one else had looked at where I provided all of the requested information. XXXX then replies to my email with " I have responded to the representative you speak with last time. Please see attached email and request. '' Although, nothing was attached to the email. After speaking to a manger of the call center, we finally got XXXX to figure out how to attach a letter to an email ( attached ). I took the letter to the DMV and was told it will work if it is notarized and an original is submitted. 

XX/XX/XXXX : Sent email to XXXX stating that the DMV needs a notarized document and that the year of the vehicle was wrong ( XXXX instead of XXXX ). I received a reply from XXXX XXXX XXXX stating " Our No interest letter does not require signature or notarization. '' I took this to the DMV and was given form REG 166 and told that HSBC will need to fill out, notarize and send me the original document. I pre-filled out REG 166 with my information and the vehicle information and sent it to XXXX. 2 hours later, I receive an email from XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ) stating : " HSBC is required by law to retain account records for 7-years. I understand your concerns were addressed with our Customer Service team on XX/XX/XXXX. Enclosed is a copy of the letter sent to you on XX/XX/XXXX in response to your request for a lien release. Im sorry for any inconvenience you may have experienced. Since there is no record of bank error, we respectfully decline your request for compensation. '' I replied : " My concerns have not been addressed and I am not sure exactly what prompted your email as I sent the below message to your titles team 2 hours ago. No letter was sent to me on XX/XX/XXXX, rather this letter was pre-dated, the titles team doesnt know how to attach a file to an email or you have the wrong information. It is my understanding that HSBC US and HSBC BANK XXXX XXXX  are one of the same origination at this point and HSBC BANK XXXX XXXX  is still a lien holder on my title. I continue to be talked to and sent messages that are only circular arguments that make no sense. The DMV will only accept a notarized document ; your no interest letter may not require notarization but the DMV has their own, which coincidently, needs to be notarized. Please see attached for REG 166 ( that I have pre-filed with the correct vehicle information ), fill out section 3 on behalf of HSBC BK XXXX XXXX have the form notarized and mail me the original. If you can not view the pdf attachment, you can find the form here : XXXX XXXX XXXX '' I am getting nowhere with this and need someone above HSBC and their internal teams to get a resolution here. At this point I feel that HSBC is abusing their power over the situation to the point of harassment ( a behavior which is intended to trouble or annoy someone, for example repeated attacks on them or attempts to cause them problems ) and insanity ( doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results ). Along with all of the email exchanges, I have had multiple phone calls ( that all went nowhere ) and made multiple trips to the DMV  to try to get this taken care of. I am not sure what else I can do as XXXX DMV is requiring a notarized document and HSBC is refusing to release the title or notarize the document.

In XXXX of XXXX I purchased a house from XXXX XXXX. This was my first house and I was not aware of all the things that went into purchasing a home. A friend of mine had a realtor they recommended and so from that suggestion, I gave her a call. I found her to be pleasant and she seemed very helpful. She works often with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) and that is who she chose to handle my loan. 
XXXX began to collect bank statements, run my credit, the works. What I didnt know, was they would have me pay off credit cards in order to get approved for the loan, money I was looking to put down on my house. There were so many things I had to pay off before I could qualify. Now this is fine, but this is the start of information they did not disclose to me. XXXX disclosed information in parts, to where it would seem I had no choice but to move forward with their recommendation. They prepared my loan and shipped it off to the highest bidder. I know this is now part of the business now, but I feel someone should have disclosed to me that I had more options than what they presented. I was approved for the loan and I have been the happy homeowner of my house for the past year and 6 months. 
Since then, Dovenmuehle has picked up my loan from XXXX and I have continued making my regular monthly payments, never late I might add. On XX/XX/XXXX of XXXX, I received a letter from Dovenmuehle staying they have not received proof of hazard insurance and they have purchased a policy to protect their interest on the property. It also advised that if I had purchased a hazard insurance policy that they would cancel the policy they obtained. This letter came as a surprise to me. During the process of getting approval for the initial loan, I was required to provide a quote to XXXX of the homeowners insurance that I was wanting to use for my home. I provided such quote from XXXX and was under the impression that the policy was purchased and was in effect for the past year and six months. Still confused, I contacted Dovenmuehle, the rep I spoke with stated that there was no hazard insurance on the property. I asked how this could be possible as I provided XXXX information when I had closed on the loan and they stated that a policy was never purchased. I asked how it was possible that a year has gone by without anyone noticing and the rep was speechless at this point. She disclosed that audits get done every XXXX and advised that one was never done on this account and stated, we forgot about you. Now, to my understanding, they are required by law to audits. Furthermore, I am not sure how I was able to close on the loan when a homeowners policy was never purchased, also a requirement to my knowledge. I never once received one email, one phone call, or letter from Dovenmuehle advising me of not having hazard insurance until XXXX of XXXX, more than 1 year later. 
This began the process of me searching for answers. I pulled out my closing documents and saw that it spells out word for word in the breakdown I was being charged {$560.00} for Homeowners Insurance Premium ( 12 mo. ) to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and the next line indicates {$140.00} also for Homeowners Insurance {$47.00} per month for 3 mo. Where did this money go if it did not go to a homeowners insurance policy? I also pulled all my monthly mortgage statements to review. Every month for the past year, according to my statements, {$230.00} has been allotted for Escrow ( taxes and insurance ) but I am not sure where that money has gone if no insurance policy was ever purchased. 
Since this homeowners policy was purchased by Dovenmuehle, as of XX/XX/XXXX, I am being required to pay an additional $ 200+ a month of back-payment because they advised I must pay for not having insurance on my home for 14 months. What happened to the money that was allotted for Escrow over that past 14 months? Where did that money go? 
I have been told by XXXX as well as Dovenmuehle, which this almost never happens. Ok great, but I am still stuck with paying extra each month until I meet the forced insurance, which is around {$1500.00} and some change. Either way I am still confused on how I got into this position. I have never missed a payment I have never been late on anything. Why did I not have insurance? How did my account get out of underwriting with no insurance? What would have happened if something catastrophic would have happened to the house? 
Around XXXX or XXXX, I received a call from XXXX XXXX from XXXX about refinancing my loan. I was familiar with XXXX, as he was the one who handled all the documents and closing when I initially received my loan from XXXX.

This would go on for about three weeks of him getting answers. XXXX never explained what had happened but advised that he would get my money reimbursed. Right off the bat, she noticed that XXXX never sent my check for {$560.00} anywhere and it sat. States that whoever put the numbers together for me did not have enough coming out for a few things.

I dont know, but he never brought this to my attention. I dont find any of this to be fair, I got the short end of the stick. I turned in every document they asked me for, I paid off debt they asked to pay before closing, I took XXXXs and Dovenmuehles advice, and it has not been in my best interest. I did my part ; I have never missed and payment and still have not missed a payment despite having to pay {$200.00} more each month because of XXXX/Dovenmuehle mistake. On XX/XX/2020, my husband and I traded in our XXXX  XXXX XXXX XXXX, which was financed through Hyundai Motor Finance. The XXXX had an extended warranty that we had purchased along with the vehicle in XXXX of the previous year. On XX/XX/2020, I contacted the dealership, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, to inquire about how we would receive a refund for this extended warranty. I was sent the required paperwork, filled it out and returned it on the same day. I was informed at that time that the refund would take approximately 60-90 days to reach us. 

After 90 days had come and gone, I first called the issuer of the warranty to inquire about the status of the refund. They informed me that they had sent the refund to Hyundai Motor Finance at the beginning of XXXX, before I had ever even requested it. I then called the dealership back to ask if they had any information for me regarding the refund. They informed me that the refund would be issued by Hyundai Motor Finance directly, and that I would need to contact them to discuss the matter. 

Before contacting Hyundai Motor Finance directly, I first logged into our account on their website and could see that there was a pending credit in the amount of {$3100.00} that began pending on XX/XX/2020. I then called Hyundai Motor Finance to inquire about this. The first call that I made regarding this refund was on XX/XX/2020. On this day, the first person I spoke with told me that an attempt to refund the money via direct deposit had been made, but that there was a problem with our bank. She told me to call my bank and see what the issue was and to call back once that issue had been resolved. I did this and called them back within the hour to make them aware that the issue had been resolved. I was informed by the person on the second phone call that the refund would be issued to our bank within 2-3 business days. I was satisfied with that. 

After that time had passed, and there was still no deposit into our bank from Hyundai Motor Finance, I called again to try and understand what the hold up was. This call was made on XX/XX/2020. On this call, I was informed that the first two people I had spoken with were incorrect and that they do not issue refund by direct deposit. The person I spoke with on this call informed me that there had been 2 emails sent to the payment processing department already, and that he was sending another regarding my issue. He told me to call back in 2-3 business days. I asked to speak with a supervisor and was informed that I was more than welcome to, but they could do nothing more for me than he did. I spoke with a supervisor anyway, and they informed me they were sending yet another email to payment processing. 

I called again on XX/XX/2020 and received the same responses : " I don't know what is taking so long. '' " There is no reason this should be taking so long. '' " We are sending an email to payment processing. '' There had, to date, been not one response from payment processing regarding the issue. 

I called again on XX/XX/2020. Again, I was met with the same responses. I again asked to speak with a supervisor. This supervisor informed me that there had still been no response from payment processing and she would send an email to them herself. She also informed me that not only is there a pending refund of {$3100.00} that has been with them since XX/XX/2020, but also, another refund in the amount of {$24.00} that has been with them since XXXX of 2020 that has also not been paid out. She sent an email to her higher up regarding this issue. She told me that it would be up to 5 business days until she received a response from payment processing, but to call back the next day anyway to see if any of the previous emails had been responded to. 

XX/XX/2020, I called, as instructed to try and get an update. The first person I spoke with told me that there has still been no response and no check number has been issued whatsoever in either amount. I asked if there was someone that I could speak with to issue a complaint. She transferred me to a supervisor. The supervisor at first informed me of the same thing. That nothing has changed. He then placed me on a brief hold to go through the account notes and told me that in the approximately 2 minutes that I was on hold, he had emailed and received a response from payment processing. He said they issued a check number yesterday ( XX/XX/2020 ) and that it was in an envelope, ready to send out. I asked him why the first person was unable to see this in my account, and why he wasn't able to see it when he looked the first time, either. He informed me that he didn't see it because he had to " dig ''. He could not give me a straight answer on when it would be mailed, or when we could expect to receive it. Instead, he told me to call back on Monday or Tuesday for another status report. I do not believe that the check has been issued, nor do I believe it is ready to mail. 

No other person had gotten a response from payment processing from XX/XX/2020 up until today XXXX XX/XX/2020 XXXX, but he was somehow able to get one in such a short amount of time. Every person I have spoken with at Hyundai Motor Finance has informed me that the payment processing department does not have phones, and there is no way to contact them other than by email, and it takes them a minimum of 2 days to respond. 

If this matter is in fact resolved before a response to this complaint, I would be happy to mark it as such, but I do want this out there, because they are a huge company and it would be ignorant of me to believe that we are the only people something like this has happened to.

state: I became involved with GoodLeap ( formerly Loanpal ) due to my sales representative XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX  from XXXX XXXX. He phoned another employee ( XXXX XXXX ) whom ran my credit and determined that GoodLeap was a good match. XXXX filled out the electronic application. It took many requests for this documentation to be provided to us to verify what was keyed in. Pressured sales tactics made us feel rushed without being given the option to do some research before making a decision. We were told " this offer is only good for today ''. Long story short, we found out that the solar equipment XXXX XXXX installed was not anywhere near capable of doing as the sales rep had stated. We learned this approximately a month after the install when we lost power for the first time. Hardly anything was backed up! We immediately began reaching out to the installation company regarding this issue. Meanwhile, GoodLeap started calling when we cancelled the very first auto draft. My husband ( XXXX XXXX ) and I both explained many times to many different goodleap employees that called the situation at hand. We made known we would not be paying for something that we didn't get. GoodLeap paid XXXX XXXX {$69000.00} for solar installation. I recall on one of the phone conversations I said " You've paid for services rendered yet those services have not been provided ''. I was informed that goodleap didn't pay for services rendered. They funded the install company for the equipment only. I found this quite interesting considering another attachment sent by goodleap to me via email showed a price for trenching .... trenching isn't done on a roof mounted system to my knowledge nor did our yard show any evidence of this been done... I have a roof mounted system... odd?? One woman I spoke with requested a case be opened to investigate the situation. We later found out the man 's name was XXXX XXXX who never got in touch with myself or my husband regarding his " Investigation ''. Without any form of communication with the exception of one anonymous text which offered no contact information, the case was closed, and the collection calls started right back up. Each time I spent roughly 20 minutes on average explaining the situation over and over nearly each morning for quite some time. My husband saw another victim of this same situation post contact information for XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) on a XXXX XXXX. This person claimed they felt like this employee was listening and genuinely trying to help. XXXX reached out and explained the situation again to this man. He then requested a second investigation be opened. This one was headed by XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX  Manager. We spoke many times and exchanged numerous emails. Sadly, she more or less said the case was being closed due to not finding any fraud. This is all after I have sent her many screenshots, screenscrolls, etc to back up what I was telling her. I even provided her with screenshots of attachments sent to me by GoodLeap that the values were even different in the breakdown chart! I explained that I was very suspicious of the electronic signatures and the apparent ability to change documents signed after the fact! She could not provide me with a statement from the sales rep that had supposedly claimed he did not tell us these things we had accused him of as part of his misrepresenting sales pitch. I questioned if she actually spoke with the rep because at this point, she was closing the case and claiming she had to go off the electronic documents, not what we were showing and apparently, not off all the documentation I spent so much time providing her through the course of several weeks. Ironically, she had never updated me before this to let me know they had responded to her initial request for contact. It took me prompting by my frustration of time being wasted with no action happening. I have asked several times to be absolved of this fraudulent loan. The loan was " cured '' pushing a payment due date out to XX/XX/2022. The installation company has since closed its doors and filed bankruptcy. I reached back out to XXXX via email on XX/XX/XXXX and again asked about cancellation as I reminded her that in her email dated XX/XX/2022 she made the comment that GoodLeap was the lender and that they could not cancel their contract unless XXXX XXXX agreed to cancel theirs first. She responded the following day ( XX/XX/XXXX ) by stating that " Unfortunately we are not able to cancel out the contract. However, a XXXX manager will be in touch regarding turning your system on ''. Notably, it would seem she got a promotion between the XXXX and the XXXX as her title was changed to reflect XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX  Manager. I will say I think I had all I could handle by this point. Months of stress caused my tolerance and patience to disappear. I responded to her email quite sarcastically and asked if the lender would also be taking over sending me an electrician for my flickering lights? Would they be sending me the check I signed a document to receive for lost pay due to the installation company standing my husband up the day he had taken off work to allow them to fix our leaking roof they caused? etc many more questions but I ended off by stating that this was supposed to be a lender. Lenders do not take on installation obligations when the company shuts down. That is not their position in this XXXX triangle and that I would not accept a replacement solar installation company to finish this set up. This was the last I had contact with her. Monday XX/XX/XXXX I received a call from GoodLeap at XXXX. This man was explaining basically the same thing she had said. He stated the name of the installation company that would be taking over getting the system going. I told him the same thing. I do not consent. I decline. I do not accept these services. He asked why and I explained it to him as briefly as I could that we had been trying to have these bogus " contracts '' cancelled since a month after install upons realization that we had been scammed. I told him that goodleap had paid this company to install and yet they closed and filed bankruptcy. I told them it would be in their best interest to file with the bankruptcy court and request those funds back from them. He said he had made notes of this and wished me luck. I have not heard anything from that company since. I have an inoperable system which we were lied to from the very beginning. We have been pushed through this process of continuing to get it going by XXXX XXXX amidst them having multiple appointments for damages they had to repair from their XXXX install crew. XXXX XXXX is not new to this situation. There are many out here just like us that have eerily similar stories. XXXX is quite well known to many as well. I'm happy to provide any evidence you would need to look into this matter. I'm not looking for anything for free. I work and I pay my bills. But I will NOT be paying this one and pray they don't wreck my credit. This has been a nightmare. I filed a complaint with the XXXX Attorney General 's office as well. I'll be doing the same for the Attorney General 's office in XXXX as this is their headquarter state. I will not keep quiet and be taken advantage of. This is wrong on so many levels. Every single employee I've dealt with has heard my story. I don't know how people can be in these types of jobs and sleep well at night. How can their conscious not be bothered?

Dear Sir or Madam, 1. XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX Account XXXX Please correct this inaccurate information on my credit report. I recently pulled my credit report from your Bureau and my attorneys and I had a chance to go over my credit report and in amazement, that you have decided to report me 30 days late on this account in XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX as wells 60 days late on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. 

I immediately disputed this information with XXXX XXXX XXXX and the results of the investigation came back " verified ''. Not only was I never late on this account, but according to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the information furnisher is required to notify me of the insertion of negative listings. Since I have disputed the lates with the creditor, and you obviously " verified '' them, I am very curious as to what kinds of " records '' you may have for this alleged account. I am very confident that you are in violation of the ( FCRA ) and ( FCBA ) sections ( 1666, 1666a. 1666b., and 1666c. ) as stated below : 1666. Correction of billing errors ( b ) Billing error ( 4 ) The creditor 's failure to reflect properly on a statement, a payment made by the obligor or a credit issued to the obligor. ( 5 ) A computation error or similar error of an accounting nature of the creditor on a statement. ( 6 ) Failure to transmit the statement required under section 1637 ( b ) of this title to the last address of the obligor which has been disclosed to the creditor, unless that address was furnished less than twenty days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement is required. ( 7 ) Any other error described in regulations of the Bureau. 1666a. Regulation of credit reports ( a ) Reports by creditor on obligor 's failure to pay amount regarded as billing error After receiving a notice from an obligor as provided in section 1666 ( a ) of this title, a creditor or his agent may not directly or indirectly threaten to report to any person adversely on the obligor 's credit rating or credit standing because of the obligor 's failure to pay the amount indicated by the obligor under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, and such amount may not be reported as delinquent to any third party until the creditor has met the requirements of section 1666 of this title and has allowed the obligor the same number of days ( not less than ten ) thereafter to make payment as is provided under the credit agreement with the obligor for the payment of undisputed amounts. ( b ) Reports by creditor on delinquent amounts in dispute ; notification of obligor of parties notified of delinquency If a creditor receives a further written notice from an obligor that an amount is still in dispute within the time allowed for payment under subsection ( a ) of this section, a creditor may not report to any third party that the amount of the obligor is delinquent because the obligor has failed to pay an amount which he has indicated under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, unless the creditor also reports that the amount is in dispute and, at the same time, notifies the obligor of the name and address of each party to whom the creditor is reporting information concerning the delinquency. ( c ) Reports by creditor of subsequent resolution of delinquent amounts A creditor shall report any subsequent resolution of any delinquencies reported pursuant to subsection ( b ) to the parties to whom such delinquencies were initially reported. 1666b. Timing of payments ( a ) Time to make payments A creditor may not treat a payment on a credit card account under an open end consumer credit plan as late for any purpose, unless the creditor has adopted reasonable procedures designed to ensure that each periodic statement including the information required by section 1637 ( b ) of this title is mailed or delivered to the consumer not later than 21 days before the payment due date. Because I take my credit very seriously, I contacted every name and account that was listed on the report. I was again very shocked by the multiple names, account numbers and figures. Included with this letter, is every letter written to those who have hampered my ability to obtain credit. I believe that any judge that looks over the report would agree that it is a violation of both the FCRA, CCPA and FACTA. The following accounts were listed on your report and I have demanded from them a full accounting and five years worth of records to see if their accounts were in violation of the FAIR CREDIT BILLING ACT ( FCBA ). We also demanded signed contracts, agreements or any legal paperwork that would tie us to the following accounts. Under the FCRA, you are required to conduct an investigation on this account if I request it. I DEMAND to see all 100 % verifiable proof that I was indeed Verifiably late on these accounts and the creditor fulfilled its obligations under ( FCBA 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) ), As I was never notified of a billing delinquency on my accounts, which the creditor must do under section ( FCBA1666 ( b ) ( 6 ). I DEMAND to see proof that I was mailed my statement to the correct address notifying me of both payment due date and delinquency of payment on the account. If you can not provide 100 % Verifiable proof and proper documentation that the CREDITOR fulfilled its obligations under the ( FCBA ) and ( FCRA ), I therefore demand these late payments be removed from my account or I will be forced to be in contact with the Attorney General of my State and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. I therefore am submitting my written request to you to conduct an investigation. Per the FCRA, you have 30 days to conduct this investigation and respond to my request. If you do not respond within this time period, per the FCRA, you must remove this negative information. Thank you for your time, XXXX XXXX SS # : XXXX Date of Birth : XX/XX/XXXX XXXX : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, Iowa XXXX

state:
I have had my Chase United Mileage Plus Credit Card for over two years. During a rough patch, I lived off the credit from that card, and although it was difficult I paid a huge price by way of interest. I never have made a late payment and have been fully accountable for what I owe Chase. 


Sometime around mid-XX/XX/2018, I received an offer from my Chase United MileagePlus Credit Card. The offer stated that, for a 3 % transaction fee, I would be given a year to pay off any balance transfers at 0 % interest, and after a year if the total of the transfers was not paid in full, I would pay all the accrued interest starting from the balance transfer authorization date. The offer claimed to be good for transfers through XX/XX/XXXX. Chase even sent me checks that I could use to make payments or, they suggested, I could write one to myself and deposit it into my checking account. I took Chase up on their offer and wrote myself a {$2000.00} check and deposited it via mobile deposit, to my XXXX XXXX checking account, on XX/XX/2018. 


On XX/XX/XXXX, just as I was leaving for a few days, I received a mobile fraud alert, from Chase, stating that an XXXX transaction for a {$0.00} authorization was made on the afternoon before, ( XX/XX/XXXX, at around XXXX XXXX ), to the aforementioned, Chase United Mileage Plus, that had offered me the promotion. Concerned, as I did not make an XXXX transaction, I immediately called the customer service number on the back of my card, to follow up on the alert. 


Although the card had not incurred charges, when I called to speak with the Chase Rep, on XX/XX/XXXX, she asked if I would like to cancel the card, as the authorization raised suspension that the card may be jeopardized. The Chase rep specifically asked about the {$2000.00} check that I had deposited to my XXXX XXXX checking account on the XXXX. I made it clear that the check for {$2000.00} was a valid transaction, and that I was depending on it, as I had already made transactions against the amount. I was told it would probably be best to cancel the card and get a new one, because my card had been jeopardized ; assured that the {$2000.00} in my XXXX XXXX checking account was secure, I agreed to cancel the card. 


When I returned home, on Saturday, XX/XX/XXXX, upon checking my email and noticing XXXX XXXX messages regarding overdraft and a returned check fees, because on XX/XX/XXXX, the very next day after being assured the {$2000.00} check was safely in my XXXX XXXX checking account, the {$2000.00} check did not clear. 


After a phone call to XXXX XXXX on, Saturday, XX/XX/XXXX, I discovered the reason that the check had not cleared was because Chase denied authorization. On XX/XX/XXXX, I made a call to Chase and spoke for 43 minutes, with a man who identified himself as XXXX, from XXXX, Missouri. For the next 43 minutes I explained that although a Chase Rep confirmed with me, on XX/XX/XXXX, that the check was legitimate and that she had assured me that the {$2000.00} would be transferred into my XXXX XXXX bank account, and did not tell me that a new credit card number would jeopardize the very vital {$2000.00} transaction, that it did not get transferred to my account. Further, I informed XXXX about the bounced rent check, the fees which, at the time, I thought totaled {$100.00}, and that it was urgent that Chase correct the situation in a timely manner, because their error had elevated my situation to crisis status. Additionally, I made a request at that time, for Chase to notify XXXX XXXX about what had taken place, on Chases end. 


XXXX explained that he had to release the {$2000.00} XXXX XXXX hold Chase had on my account before the transfer could be made. This confused me, as I am not sure why the hold remained if Chase would not authorize the transaction. He continued by saying that the release would be processed by, Monday, XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX asked and I confirmed that the XXXX XXXX account where I had attempted to deposit the {$2000.00} check, was the same account registered with Chase.com, and the account that I have used for all but a few payments to Chase, for over two years. 


Because XXXX XXXX and Chase accounts had already established a connection, XXXX explained that if I would call on Monday, XX/XX/XXXX, the {$2000.00} transfer to the XXXX XXXX account could easily be done over the phone with any Chase representative. Regarding the fees charged to my XXXX XXXX Checking account, when I offered to send proof of the charges, XXXX said it would not be necessary to send proof and the only thing he could do is credit my Chase account {$100.00}. I did not think this was acceptable, as the fees were from my checking account, and if I tried to access the fees Chase had caused, now I would have to pay at least 3 percent to do so. 


XXXX made it clear that crediting my Chase account {$100.00}, was the only way I would see any kind of reimbursement of the fees I suffered because of Chases poor customer service and misleading information. Further, although XXXX said he would see what he could do about notifying XXXX XXXX, he never made good on fulfilling my request. Still XXXX XXXX has heard nothing from Chase, nor has Chase offered me any documentation to give XXXX XXXX. 


With increasing anxiety, I could not wait to handle this on Monday, XX/XX/XXXX. Before I called Chase to make the transaction, I logged into my account. On XX/XX/XXXX, after logging into my account, I found that there was 1 external  bank fee credit added to my Chase account, in the amount of {$5.00}. I called Chase and the first person I spoke with was XXXX. 


XXXX had XXXX notes and when she explained that it would take 3 -7 business days for the {$2000.00} transfer to show up at XXXX XXXX, I became frustrated and explained that I was told because the two accounts had already established a connection, that it would facilitate an easy transfer, just as I had been told, by XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. I begged and pleaded for her to figure out a way to make this transfer happen that same day, as it was now dire and I was suffering from a financial domino effect. 


Before demanding to speak with her supervisor, I told her about the {$100.00} credit that XXXX had said he would make to my account, and that only one credit for {$5.00}, showed on my account activity. XXXX insisted that the {$100.00} had been credited to my account, on XX/XX/XXXX, she even went as far to tell me that two different transactions had taken place one for {$100.00} and one for {$5.00}. I told her she was not correct, as I was, at that very moment looking at my account activity online and the {$100.00} credit was not there. She swore that the money had been credited to my account. I also made the plea that Chase notify XXXX XXXX of the situation and she flat out refused to do so, saying that it would not be necessary. After arguing back and forth for a while, I finally asked to speak with another supervisor, hoping that someone would see that, because of this uniquely urgent situation, Chase might want to do the right thing after causing such overwhelming stress and financial jeopardy. I was transferred to XXXX XXXX. 


XXXX admitted that I had been given false or at least less than thorough information, by multiple Chasse representatives. Further he told me he could understand why I was so upset but made no effort to figure out a helpful way to expedite the {$2000.00} transfer in an urgent manner, and again told me it would take 3 to 7 business days before the money would be transferred into my XXXX XXXX account. Before ending the 1 hour and 35 minute phone call, XXXX said no reimbursement would be made until I offered proof that the fees had been deducted from my account, even after XXXX had told me that the money had been credited to my account. 


I was more than happy to supply XXXX with the information he requested and he said that after I supplied the information to verify my fees, he would have the money deposited to my XXXX XXXX checking account. I was more pleased with this, as I had felt disrespected when XXXX, on XX/XX/XXXX, told me the only way I could receive reimbursement was to be forced to apply the funds to my credit card. Furious, I asked XXXX to check the phone calls from XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, to validate that over and over Chase had manipulated and misinformed me after jeopardizing my financial security. He said that he believed me, that the calls were recorded for training purposes to support future customer service practice, but would not be used to support my issues. 


Through tears, I pleaded with XXXX to tell me why it was ok to allow all of this to happen to mewhy had the Chase reps all lied to me. XXXX said he was sorry and that, it was not our intention to lie to you. 


Yesterday, XX/XX/XXXX, I logged on to Chase to find that a {$100.00} credit had been added to my Chase credit card account. I believe that Chase acted fraudulently by backdating this credit, as the activity states the account was credited on XX/XX/XXXX, it was not. Not only do I have a copy of the activity proving so, when I spoke with XXXX, today XX/XX/XXXX to let her know I planned on taking further action regarding the manner, she said that the {$100.00} was credited on XX/XX/XXXX. 


That Chase would do NOTHING to assist helping a customer in crisis made at their hand, but went to the trouble to commit fraud by backdating a {$100.00} credit to cover a lie that was told to me by their customer service representative, XXXX, that wouldnt have mattered anyway because XXXX XXXX gave his word that after sending the documents, proving the charged fees, the money would be transferred back over to my XXXX XXXX account. 


On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent in the XXXX XXXX documents that showed fee charges to prove where Chase had cost me significant damage, along with a lengthy letter describing the details of this matter, much like this letter I am sending you. A reply saying that they would respond within 14 business days is beyond borderlines abuse, in my opinion. 


Also, on XX/XX/XXXX, I checked the status of my balance transfer, it is not expected to take place until XX/XX/XXXX, which makes me wonder why on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX went out of his way to explain the ease of getting the funds to XXXX XXXX, given the established connection between the two accounts. I dont believe anyone from Chase anymore. I would be foolish to do so. I believe that Chase should be guilty of fraud, regarding the backdated credit adjustment to my account. Their malicious behavior is a threat to all of their clients, as if they are willing to lie about something so insignificant, there is no telling how much people have truly suffered at their hand. 
I intend to follow through with legal action, if there is any that can be taken. 


A strange turn of events this morning, XX/XX/XXXX, where my wallet was stolen sometime after I had bought groceries at XXXX, with cash, and I was forced to cancel all of my credit cards. A fraudulent charge had been made to XXXX from the aforementioned Chase account. I called and reported the abuse. When XXXX XXXX said she would cancel my card and be sending me a new one I sobbed in terror, and told her that the {$2000.00} transfer would be jeopardized and I had basically already spent the money, and told her about the trauma I suffered, she assured me that she could make an adjustment to be sure that the transfer would go through. Of all the people I spoke to with Chase, she seemed to be the most understanding, thorough and accurate professional. She gave me her full name, told me that she would make an adjustment allowing the transfer to process and follow up, in the next 6 hours, via email. 


You would think this would give me peace, but it reveals that Chase could have made an adjustment to the original {$2000.00} transfer, which shows neglect, or incompetence, in addition to falsifying their statements on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, that because the credit card number had been changed, there was no way to make good on the {$2000.00} deposited to the XXXX XXXX XXXX account, XXXX said someone could have made an adjustment, but no one had. 


Where things are, at XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX  1. As of this morning, I had been charged {$150.00} in overdraft and NSF, as well as $ 300+ overdrawn with my XXXX XXXX bank account. 
2. A visit to Chases website revealed that my transfer will take another 11 days, far more than 3 to 7, which both XXXX and XXXX had estimated 3. My {$1200.00} rent check written on the XXXX was denied, $ XXXX/day late fee every day after the XXXX ; and maybe NSF charge from my landlord 4. I  Have been on a financial and emotional roller coaster due to misinformation from Chase customer service representatives who have not done anything to go out of their way to compensate or make up for their error, ( although I believe XXXX XXXX might have corrected this had I spoke to her on XX/XX/XXXX or XX/XX/XXXX ) 5. After desperate pleas of urgency and over 3 hours of phone conversations with reps, I asked that, and am awaiting : a. The {$2000.00} transfer be quickly expedited b. Someone from Chase contact XXXX XXXX to explain misunderstanding c. Concern for fees that might incur due to a - {$300.00} checking account balance 6. Wait overwhelmed with stress and fear that a reoccurring payment from my checking account may happen before Chase transfers the funds, thus resulting in further charges. ( This has already happened twice ) Chase Ethics 1. On XX/XX/XXXX, after I okd the {$2000.00} transfer with Chase, they still failed to authorize the transaction. As a financial institution, I would expect Chase to be able to meet their promotional promise. That Chase cant manage a transaction made on an established two year account, simply because there was a change on the credit card number brings into question either a. Competence, or b. unwillingness to go the extra mile after inconveniencing a customer that has shown good faith, with a has consistent payment history 2. On the XXXX, XXXX assured me that because the XXXX XXXX XXXX account had been established with Chase, via XXXX, and been a source for my Chase cc payments, the transfer could easily be completed and swiftly expedited, over the phone on Monday XX/XX/XXXX this was not accurate. 
7. Chase has offered no documentation or attempt to call XXXX XXXX on my behalf, after I asked at least two of their reps to please do so 8. On  Monday XX/XX/XXXX,, both XXXX and then XXXX said I had to wait 3 to 7 business days for the transfers eligibility to be confirmed, and that there was no possible way to get the funds to my account that day, on in an urgent manner. 
9. XXXX had assured me that, even though I only saw a {$5.00} credit to my Chase account for the external bank fee, the {$100.00} had been credited to my Chase account on XX/XX/XXXX, ; when she transferred my call, XXXX made it clear that the money would be transferred to my XXXX XXXX account, only after I supplied proof of the fees that I had been charged. 


I am a reasonable person, I make mistakes, I understand others do as well and that things happen that were not meant to cause intentional harm. I dont take any of this personal, but the unprofessional way this was handled is unacceptable, unethical, and manipulative, and I dare say fraudulent. 


When I expressed urgency and asked why I was given inaccurate information, from Chase on 3 separate occasions, I was told that though I was justified for being angry, It was not our intention to lie. I would prefer that my financial intuitions intentionally did not lie to me, and I am shocked by the entitlement of Chase, and want to take any action available to hold them responsible for their poor customer service practice and aloof willingness to act fraudulently on such an insignificant matter.

I am ( at least attempting ) to be part of the public service loan forgiveness program. 

Because my employer helps me with my payment due each month, I have multiple payments each month that come in at different times to satisfy my monthly balance. Due to this scattered payment, I have tried multiple times to get guidance on what payments count in order to ensure my total payments are qualifying each month and I am not making excess payments that dont count towards forgiveness. 

The only regulatory requirement about the timing of the 120 payments is that they not be made later than 15 days past the due date, but I have been told that some of my bill satisfying payments may not be qualifying because they were made too early. I have been told completely inconsistent policies regarding early payments by different representatives and every time I ask for a written policy so that I can fully understand and ensure I am complying with it, I am told no written policy exists. 

After my number of qualifying payments reported by the XXXX XXXX  was far lower than the number I believed I had made, I promptly sought clarification. I was told the only way to review this was to make a formal request for a review of payments and wait for the company to complete a unilateral review that would take an entire year. This review would not provide any transparency or allow me to have a discussion with a human doing a review, all while 12 months of potentially qualifying payments pass while I am potentially still not making qualifying payments despite satisfying every bill because no one can provide me with a clear understanding of what the early paying policy for a monthly bill actually is. 

This lack of transparency and failure to communicate requirements that end up disqualifying payments that public service workers are diligently making on their monthly bills completely defeats the purpose of this program and discourages program participation.

I was advised to contact my bank- XXXX XXXX. I contacted XXXX XXXX and explained the situation and they assisted with a stop future payment request on XX/XX/XXXX. 

On XX/XX/year> I discovered that XXXX XXXX inadvertently stopped the original payment scheduled on XX/XX/XXXX for XX/XX/XXXX ( although is was pending with the bank ) and the XXXX payment I did not authorize. After this discovery, I submitted another payment for XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX via Mohela 's website to ensure I received credit for XXXX. 

The above describes a series of events that result in confusion and mistrust. My complaint is that Mohela should not process payments that you do not authorize and should be able to provide supporting documentation when this occurs ( when was the payment submitted, how, email confirmation documenting the payment, etc ) all of which they could not provide. I feel that this is attempt to cause confusion and not provide payment credit within a reasonable time for individuals who are near loan forgiveness and deduct additional payments that are not authorized. My loans have been in good standing and I have a systematic process to ensure my payments are made before the due date. A review of my payments via Mohela 's new platform reflects that all my payments are made on the XXXX of the month. 

In addition, it is not clear why Mohela does not update payments monthly with Federal Student Aid when every other merchant ( credit cards vendors, utility providers, etc. ) are expected to provide updates on accounts on a monthly basis via monthly account statements that reflect payments made to-date and the amount owed. Further, there is also the practice of duplicating the amount owed for student loans on your credit report. Last month my student loan amount was duplicated on my XXXX credit report ( I owe ~ $ XXXX and the loan was listed twice indicating that I was XXXX in debt more than I am ) I submitted a dispute and received a " no change/update '' response but the issue seemed to have resolved on its on but the fact that it happened is gravely concerning as these practices require diligent observation, recording and record keeping on behalf of the consumer when organizations such as Mohela should be practicing ethically. 

As I prepared to submit this complaint today I have also noticed that the XXXX messages I sent via the Mohela 's Inbox Message feature on XX/XX/XXXX are no longer showing on the website. One email was sent to request cancellation of the XXXX payment I noticed and did not authorize and requested an explanation regarding while I awaited a return call from Mohela ( sent just in case they did not call me back ). The second email was sent after I utilized the chat feature on Federal Student Aid website to inquire about how my payments could be update. The chat transcripts reflects that I was advised to to contact my loan servicer, Mohela to request that they " push '' my most up-to-date payments to Federal Student Aid as it is the loan servicer 's responsibility to provide updates. I have documentation from XX/XX/year> that reflect that I received credit for my XXXX payment in XXXX so it is uncertain why the reporting has changed. I have noted the lag time reflected in the XXXX transcript but this is unacceptable. 

My regret is that I did not take screenshots of all activities specifically the emails sent via Mohela 's Inbox Email messaging platform - I never would have thought the organization would go so low by deleting documentation but here we are.

XXXX told me the loan was a lease, but ended up not being a lease ( I later learned ) and to come back after a year to 18 months they would put me in a different Toyota with a better interest rate.

Finally someone told me that he had passed away, and that the XXXX XXXX I was in was not a lease as had been explained, but instead a purchase at a high interest rate. I am on a fixed income as a 100 % XXXX vet and recently ran into some financial difficulties. 

From the inception of the last agreement with Toyota I paid anywhere from $ XXXX a month extra toward the loan included in the autodraft payment to reduce the principal on the loan. When I tried to get another vehicle I was told that stock wasn't available at the time due to a chip shortage, even in XXXX and throughout XXXX. 

I was attempting to get something at a lower interest rate, thinking it was ending the lease to purchase a new XXXX at a better interest rate than what I had been paying since roughly XXXX or XX/XX/XXXX. 

The vehicle was repossessed in late XXXX or XXXX of XXXX. I was fortunate, that the vehicle wasn't sold at auction prior to XX/XX/XXXX and through Toyota representatives and XXXX XXXX I paid in urgency fees and money orders for repossession, storage and past due payments, an approximate total of {$3500.00} While attempting to recover my personal belongings, through XXXX XXXX, a third party repossession and recovery service that I would have to pay money to recover clothing, paperwork or other personal items from my vehicle. This occurred over the phone, and was told to me by a woman that answered the phone for that business. 

I then told her that the toyota representative informed me less than XXXX hours prior to my call with her, that I was not to pay any fees for acquiring my personal belongings. 

I also had contacted TDLR ( Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation ) to determine whether or not recovery and repossession companies fell under the same regulatory guidelines as towing vehicle companies do. TDLR told me they don't regulate recovery and repossession businesses. 

I was at a loss, because seemingly so, these companies charge consumers whatever they want, and are not available during normal business hours of XXXX Monday through Friday or even after hours in which consumers XXXX acquire their belongings from recovered vehicles. 

After navigating the website, from XXXX XXXX, unsuccessfully, and speaking to the same woman, I was told which buttons to press onscreen that seemingly had no connection to my situation or vehicle, but was a necessary part of their convoluted process to acquire my belongings. 

The appointment was made and upon arrival I noticed that the property didn't appear to be a business in the operation of anything, and seemingly just a location with a XXXX foot fence surrounding interior portions of the property. XXXX sign on an exterior corner wall had faded out words, and was missing the standard verbiage on display at towing facilities in Texas. 

I was only able to make the appointment on the phone and avoid fees to recover my property because I told the woman on the phone that Toyota told me to tell them they weren't supposed to charge me to acquire my belongings. It seemed as if, since Toyota told me that at the onset, that they are aware consumers are routinely charged erroneous fees by XXXX XXXX services located at the edge of XXXX and XXXX XXXX Texas ; otherwise why would they mention it and why would the receptionist or admin staff at XXXX tell me I had to pay those fees, and then change their mind after I as a consumer tell them the lending company, Toyota said I was not obligated to do so. 

After numerous attempts on XX/XX/XXXX using XXXX XXXX and paying over {$3500.00} in payments, consisting of XXXX separate transactions Toyota told me my loan was reinstated and they'd sent a hold to XXXX XXXX, to prevent the auction of my XXXX XXXX XXXX. This occured prior to XXXX on that date. That amount included the repossession fee, storage and transportation from XXXX to XXXX XXXX ( auction facility ). After paying that, I was then told that I would also need to pay additional storage, in the amount of roughly {$10.00} a day plus other fees, perhaps taxes, they were unsure. I spoke to numerous representatives at XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, and the XXXX as they and Toyota instructed me to do. They as of yet, XXXX pm, central, have been unable to tell me what that amount is, or even when I can make an appointment to acquire the vehicle, and that they don't make appointments the day of hold received or redemption forms from the lender. It appears this business practice is merely a way of taking more money from consumers, who are likely already struggling financially, via undue delays, and business practices in which lenders and auction service companies don't communicate in any way, that facilitates or enables a modicum of standard business financial services. 

So far today, I've made XXXX phone calls in an attempt to schedule an appointment with XXXX XXXX, who again doesn't allow consumers to acquire redeemed properties the day they receive the paperwork from lenders allowing consumers to acquire their property after reinstating loans. I also made no less than XXXX phone calls between Toyota and XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. 

I am concerned that during this loan, which was said to be a lease and not to worry about anything, to trade up the year after the acquisition of the XXXX XXXX, was a ploy to entangle me or contractually engage me, in business with toyota motor credit, for not just two to three years, but more like 5 to 8 years if the deal had went through as initially explained and guaranteeing Toyota monies from me through what would have been XX/XX/XXXX, ( date of first lease/loan payment ) and into another loan, with a standard average of 60 months would've been XXXX or XXXX. 

I am concerned that there were fees and or un-necessary expenditures embedded in the paperwork for the XXXX XXXX that resulted in longer payment periods, and that perhaps I was victim to the procedures or policies of toyota motor credit, that resulted in the lawsuit from the CFBP against toyota ( and resulted in a judgement of {$60.00} million against Toyota Motor Credit ), because of all the nuances and exceedingly difficult hurdles already mentioned, that I encountered while dealing with Toyota, XXXX, and XXXX. 

It seems as if lending corporations, recovery and repossession services work in concert to extort and entangle consumers in processes that only facilitate the enrichment and financial gains of Americans facing financial hardships. It has been almost impossible thus far to navigate this process no one at any company has been able to provide an actual fact based answer, or solution. 

Due to this, I lost the ability to generate income for utilities, food, rent, and other necessity items because it was my only mode of transportation. I was without electricity, water, food and through the grace of my landlord at the last moment was granted a reprieve on the court ordered eviction he'd already submitted. 

After navigating this process and viewing the court details that were publicly available it seems as if, from an outside perspective looking in through the lens of an affected consumer that their business practices and that of their partners is just a smaller piece of the puzzle that allowed them to generate additional income, while ensuring future financial successes for the corporation, their vendors, and 3rd party service providers.

New flood zone maps were being drawn up for our city and went into effect XX/XX/XXXX. When we heard there was a good possibility that our home would now be considered in the flood zone and would be required to purchase flood insurance, we hired XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX. to come to the property and take measurements. When he finished measuring my property his exact words to me were, " It's not even close. '' XXXX created a Letter of Map Amendment ( LOMA ) and filed it with FEMA. It went into effect XX/XX/XXXX. 

Our mortgage with XXXX XXXX  was sold to PNC Bank XX/XX/XXXX. PNC sent us letters on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX stating that we were in the flood zone and would be required to purchase insurance. When we did not purchase flood insurance on our own they purchased it on our behalf. We faxed the LOMA to PNC Bank XX/XX/XXXX. 

I received a certified letter from PNC dated XX/XX/XXXX stating they reviewed our insurance inquiry but flood insurance was still required. I called PNC and talked to XXXX. She said that the map was dated XX/XX/XXXX and the LOMA was dated XX/XX/XXXX. I called FEMA and talked to XXXX. He said that the maps went into effect XX/XX/XXXX and the LOMA was dated XX/XX/XXXX and that the LOMA was valid. I called PNC back and talked to XXXX. I explained that I had talked to FEMA and maybe PNC had the dates backwards. 

I received another certified letter from PNC dated XX/XX/XXXX stating that they reviewed our insurance inquiry but the FEMA website has a map with our property in a flood zone. They included a few maps as well as a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Form prepared by XXXX. On this form in section B, box 3 it asks " Is there a Letter of Map Change ( LOMC )? '' They had selected " No. '' I called FEMA again and asked him to review the map and LOMA. " What am I missing? '' I asked. He said, " Your letter is valid and is a legally binding document. If they ignore it, they are in violation. You should report them to the Lending Institution Regulatory Authority. '' XX/XX/XXXX, I called PNC and talked to XXXX. She assured me that she would personally find out what is going on and call me back in 2-3 days. Frankly, I don't understand what they are researching since they should know why they rejected my paperwork twice. In my opinion this " research '' should already have been done if they felt they had grounds to reject the LOMA again and it should be noted on my file. I took a picture of my letter from our previous lender ( XXXX XXXX ) stating that they would refund our flood insurance since we were not in the flood zone according to the LOMA and sent it to PNC. I never heard back from XXXX. 

I called PNC and talked to XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. He said, " I see your letter. I will forward that on to the flood review department. You should hear back by XX/XX/XXXX. '' XX/XX/XXXX I called PNC to make sure things are progressing. I talked to XXXX who told me that according to her records they have until XX/XX/XXXX to get back to me. I explained my frustrations : I have called them five times. I have called FEMA twice. Our land surveyor says that the LOMA is a matter of public record and should have been reviewed by the PNC underwriters before they even decided to purchase our loan. FEMA suggested that I report them. The land surveyor, FEMA, and our previous lender all  determined that we were not in the flood zone and not required to purchase flood insurance. I want to talk to a supervisor. 

XXXX said they will need 24-48 hours to get back to me. I told her, " I have waited long enough. I want to talk to someone today. '' No one contacted me. 

XX/XX/XXXX, I called PNC 's customer service department. I talked to XXXX and asked her, " Who do I talk to about a complaint? '' I explained the situation to her. She said she would review everything, find out what's going on, and call me back that day. I called customer service just before closing to see if XXXX had any answers for me. I talked to XXXX who said that a supervisor from PNC insurance department will be calling me tomorrow. 

This is terrible customer service. If I had a choice I would take my business elsewhere. If there is a problem with the paperwork, a courtesy phone call would have been appreciated. These letters that they sent me don't tell me what the problem is - just that I should talk to FEMA which I have twice. They don't see any problems. I can't get through the front line of telephone operators at PNC to get to a person with any answers. This entire experience has been very frustrating. Most of the employees that answer the phone apologize and sympathize with me but I can't get any results. 

XX/XX/XXXX I wait anxiously for the 48 hour deadline to hear from a supervisor. It comes and goes. I call PNC insurance department. I wish I had the name of this employee because she was the most cold and unhelpful person I've encountered during this ordeal. She said in a snarky tone, " It's not 48 literal hours. We have until the end of business today to contact you. '' So now, yes, I'm angry. I'm beyond frustrated. I raised my voice. While I tried to explain that I was in the process of reporting them because it was getting ridiculous, she talked over me and said she would disconnect the call unless I stopped yelling. 

" Did you hear what I said? I'm going to report your bank because I can't get any answers to this problem, '' I repeated now calmer. " Well that's your right, '' she said. " You don't even care. I have called many times and talked to many people and no one has talked to me the way you have, '' I said. " You were probably respectful to them and you have not been respectful to me, '' she claimed. She ended with, " I will call you back at XXXX today to make sure that a supervisor has called you. '' I didn't hear back from anyone that day. 

XX/XX/XXXX, an executive calls me I think because of my complaint to the customer service department. He apologizes for all the hassle I've been through. I tell him my story. He says, " We have to do whatever FEMA says. '' I said, " Good because FEMA says the LOMA is valid and that you are in violation. '' He goes looking through the paperwork and finds the faxed LOMA. He tells me that it's very grainy and he can't read most of it. I offer to email him a picture of the document. He said to give him 2-3 days to get this figured out. 

XX/XX/XXXX, the supervisor for the insurance department calls. I give him an abbreviated version of what I've been going through. He apologizes and says that's not what they want to hear from customers. He mentioned the problem with the dates. Dear Sir or Madam, 1. ONEMAIN Account Number:XXXX  Please correct this inaccurate information on my credit report. I recently pulled my credit report from your Bureau and my attorneys and I had a chance to go over my credit report and in amazement, that you have decided to report me 30 days late on this account in XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. 
I immediately disputed this information with ONEMAIN and the results of the investigation came back " verified ''. Not only was I never late on this account, but according to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the information furnisher is required to notify me of the insertion of negative listings. Since I have disputed the lates with the creditor, and you obviously " verified '' them, I am very curious as to what kinds of " records '' you may have for this alleged account. I am very confident that you are in violation of the ( FCRA ) and ( FCBA ) sections ( 1666, 1666a. 1666b., and 1666c. ) as stated below : 1666. Correction of billing errors ( b ) Billing error ( 4 ) The creditor 's failure to reflect properly on a statement, a payment made by the obligor or a credit issued to the obligor. ( 5 ) A computation error or similar error of an accounting nature of the creditor on a statement. ( 6 ) Failure to transmit the statement required under section 1637 ( b ) of this title to the last address of the obligor which has been disclosed to the creditor, unless that address was furnished less than twenty days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement is required. ( 7 ) Any other error described in regulations of the Bureau. 1666a. Regulation of credit reports ( a ) Reports by creditor on obligor 's failure to pay amount regarded as billing error After receiving a notice from an obligor as provided in section 1666 ( a ) of this title, a creditor or his agent may not directly or indirectly threaten to report to any person adversely on the obligor 's credit rating or credit standing because of the obligor 's failure to pay the amount indicated by the obligor under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, and such amount may not be reported as delinquent to any third party until the creditor has met the requirements of section 1666 of this title and has allowed the obligor the same number of days ( not less than ten ) thereafter to make payment as is provided under the credit agreement with the obligor for the payment of undisputed amounts. ( b ) Reports by creditor on delinquent amounts in dispute ; notification of obligor of parties notified of delinquency If a creditor receives a further written notice from an obligor that an amount is still in dispute within the time allowed for payment under subsection ( a ) of this section, a creditor may not report to any third party that the amount of the obligor is delinquent because the obligor has failed to pay an amount which he has indicated under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, unless the creditor also reports that the amount is in dispute and, at the same time, notifies the obligor of the name and address of each party to whom the creditor is reporting information concerning the delinquency. ( c ) Reports by creditor of subsequent resolution of delinquent amounts A creditor shall report any subsequent resolution of any delinquencies reported pursuant to subsection ( b ) to the parties to whom such delinquencies were initially reported. 1666b. Timing of payments ( a ) Time to make payments A creditor may not treat a payment on a credit card account under an open end consumer credit plan as late for any purpose, unless the creditor has adopted reasonable procedures designed to ensure that each periodic statement including the information required by section 1637 ( b ) of this title is mailed or delivered to the consumer not later than 21 days before the payment due date. Because I take my credit very seriously, I contacted every name and account that was listed on the report. I was again very shocked by the multiple names, account numbers and figures. Included with this letter, is every letter written to those who have hampered my ability to obtain credit. I believe that any judge that looks over the report would agree that it is a violation of both the FCRA, CCPA and FACTA. The following accounts were listed on your report and I have demanded from them a full accounting and five years worth of records to see if their accounts were in violation of the FAIR CREDIT BILLING ACT ( FCBA ). We also demanded signed contracts, agreements or any legal paperwork that would tie us to the following accounts. Under the FCRA, you are required to conduct an investigation on this account if I request it. I DEMAND to see all 100 % verifiable proof that I was indeed Verifiably late on these accounts and the creditor fulfilled its obligations under ( FCBA 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) ), As I was never notified of a billing delinquency on my accounts, which the creditor must do under section ( FCBA1666 ( b ) ( 6 ). I DEMAND to see proof that I was mailed my statement to the correct address notifying me of both payment due date and delinquency of payment on the account. If you can not provide 100 % Verifiable proof and proper documentation that the CREDITOR fulfilled its obligations under the ( FCBA ) and ( FCRA ), I therefore demand these late payments be removed from my account or I will be forced to be in contact with the Attorney General of my State and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. I therefore am submitting my written request to you to conduct an investigation. Per the FCRA, you have 30 days to conduct this investigation and respond to my request. If you do not respond within this time period, per the FCRA, you must remove this negative information. Thank you for your time, XXXX XXXX SS # : XXXX Date of Birth : XX/XX/XXXX XXXX : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX, Iowa XXXX

I have already tried resolving this problem with AMEX ( ref : XXXX-XXXX  ) and here is the previous summary : ( A ) : Submitted on XX/XX/XXXX : I have been a customer of American Express ( AMEX ) consumer cards since XX/XX/XXXX but was the receiving end of few dubious practices. Here is the chronology of event ( s ). 1. In XX/XX/XXXX, we started a XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX dba   XXXX ) with three partners and applied for business card ( s ) for the same. 2. As part of the application process, AMEX asked several questions about the business - nature of legal entity, license number, employees, expected spend, topline revenue etc. 3. Eventually the card ( ending XXXX ) was issued to partners and few of our employees, the most we spent on the card was about $ 15k in a month and always paid our bills on time. 4. In XX/XX/XXXX, the business hit a few snags and the legal entity dissolved and there was {$3400.00} due on the AMEX card at the time of dissolution of LLC. 5. In late XX/XX/XXXX, AMEX customer support team called me and literally threatened me that all the dues will be reported against my personal credit and essentially froze all my personal cards where I was paying bills on time. 6. I asked the customer rep that no personal information ( like SSN ) was asked in step-2 so what gave AMEX rights to attach business card of a LLC to my personal account. The rep had no answer and suggested opening a ticket to inquire with their IT team to get details of application sign up session. I agreed to the recommendation as I wanted to be fair to AMEX as well. 7. In order to avoid further escalation, I paid the dues and clearly told AMEX customer service rep that I am waiting to get details of my explicit consent to attach a business card to my personal account. 8. It has been almost 6 weeks, I have called them twice ( XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX ) and the customer service rep answering does not seem to recall any details from the previous conversation and AMEX has not furnished any proof of my explicit consent. This is a predatory practice from AMEX that has harmed me and possibly many other small business owners : 1. AMEX essentially overrode the LLC structure of business by flashing a 15-page PDF with relevant clauses buried somewhere in the fine font. 2. Nowhere during the online application process AMEX explicitly declared prominently that the credit card was issued on a personal guarantee. If personal gurantee was all that AMEX cared for, then the application process should have highlighted this fact prominently instead of burying it in fine print. 3. We even issued cards to partners and other employees thereby exposing myself to a huge financial risk as I was unaware that the credit card is my sole financial responsibility. 4. Even after repeated attempts, AMEX has not been able to provide following information about the card application : a ) Date and time of credit card application b ) IP address of my machine c ) SSN number filled out on the application form.

( B ) : AMEX 's response on XX/XX/XXXX : We have completed our research and have attached a copy of our response for your review. 

( C ) : I have sent the form AMEX sent duly filled out and sent back on XX/XX/XXXX Since then it has been over three months and there is not even an acknowledgement from AMEX. So the summary of this whole things is as follows : 1. AMEX waived my right to litigate in their T & Cs 2. AMEX used predartory practices to push a business card and shoved the " peronal liability '' part somewhere in the fine print. 
3. I never provided any personal information or even agreed to bear the liability of business account on my personal credit.

4. AMEX flexed its muscle and threatened to destroy my personal credit for which I never consented.

5. When I filed complaint with CFPB about AMEX and asked that if AMEX to provide IP address, day, time and SSN number filled out at the time of busiess credit card application.

6. AMEX closed the resolution on pretext of sending me paper forms that essentially requests the same information as ( 5 ) and have not responded for over three months.

AMEX first indulged in predatory practices and now they are indulging in diversionary and delaying tactics.
