I then called LoanStar to inform them that I was having difficulty cashing the check, they proceeded to tell me to try a different bank. Upon doing so I received the same result from a different XXXX XXXX. I then proceeded to deposit it into my bank account with XXXX via the mobile app due to it was XXXX XXXX and the banks close at XXXX XXXX, and it was accepted and then later denied and placed on an administrative hold. I called my banks customer service number only to find out that my account was immediately placed on hold and was frozen due to the system could not verify the validity of the check from LoanStar. The customer service rep with XXXX then proceeded to inform me that more than likely the check will be returned and they would not be able to process it. I called LoanStar back and spoke with XXXX and XXXX to explain to them what happened and XXXX suggested that I should just cash the check at a regular check cashing place and that no one has experienced issues with cashing their checks in the past. By this time, 3 banks, including my bank had rejected the check and I needed the funds to cover funeral expenses. I didn't know what to do next, so I decided to wait to see what will process overnight. The next day, XX/XX/XXXX, I attempted to use my debit card and it declined and said invalid account on the POS system. I called my bank to see why my debit card declined and I was informed that my account was still frozen and the rep proceeded to tell me that my account had been closed due a fraudulent check that was deposited the day before. The fraud department was closed and would not open again until Tuesday, XX/XX/XXXX due to the XXXX was XXXX 's XXXX. I proceeded to go to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX on XXXX since it was the closest location to where I was at the time and explained to the teller my situation. She asked me if I had already cashed the check at another check cashing location and I answered, no. She proceeded to submit the check to her corporate office and it came back approved to proceed with the cashing process. Fast forward to XX/XX/2023 and I received a called from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX corporate office and XXXX proceeded to inform me that the check that I'd cashed from LoanStar ( Wellshire Financing ) was returned as already being cashed. My account with XXXX was still frozen and the check had not cleared my account and again I was informed that it was on an administrative hold due to the check was not verifiable. XXXX 's is asking for their money back and nothing had cleared with my bank, and it looks as though I would be out of pocket {$2500.00} with a closed account and not able to access any of my payroll or deposited funds. I had kept in touch with LoanStar throughout this ordeal and there wasn't much help provided other than XXXX forwarding me a copy of what appeared to be a cleared check from his bank. I thought the cleared check was from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX due to this was the only place that successfully cashed the check. In mid XXXX, my XXXX account was finally restored and they manually released the {$2500.00} check that was submitted via mobile deposit. I then contacted XXXX on the XXXX to setup with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to set up a time for me to come by and disburse the released funds. She'd informed me that it would be an additional {$30.00} for the returned check. On XX/XX/XXXX, for no reason and without any explanation, LoanStar towed my car away. I thought it had been stolen so I reported it as such. Upon speaking to LoanStar, they towed it because they said I was extremely late on my payment, which the payment was just due on Sunday, XX/XX/XXXX. I called into their office on XX/XX/XXXX and informed XXXX that my payment would be a little late on the XXXX due to I had just recently regained access to my banking account again and she stated that my account would be notated and that there would be a late fee accessed, and I stated that this would not be a problem. By this time, I did not have transportation and I had been in constant communication with LoanStar 's travelling Supervisor in which she proceeded to inform me that their legal office actually towed my vehicle due to the check being cashed at XXXX 's and that they had to pay XXXX 's check themselves. I had been in contact with XXXX at XXXX 's and she informed me that this was not the case. On XX/XX/XXXX, I went into LoanStar and paid the entire balance off and was handed my title to the vehicle and XXXX informed me that her supervisor would contact the towing company with the lien release for me to be able to pick up my vehicle. I proceeded to the towing company, XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX, TX, only to be informed that LoanStar had in fact ordered my car to be auctioned off on XX/XX/XXXX ; less than 7 days after towing my vehicle. I called LoanStar back and spoke with XXXX again and she then proceeded to tell me that " Oh yeah, we ordered this yesterday, " I'm sorry, my system didn't update while you were here ''. I called the auction location and they informed me that LoanStar needed to release the vehicle, in which LoanStar refused to do so even after I paid the account in full.

I have the XXXX Credit Card with Chase Bank. OnXX/XX/19, I was charged my {$75.00} annual fee for my card. On XX/XX/19, I called to request an upgrade to the XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX which has a {$95.00} annual fee. I was told that they would be crediting my {$75.00} fee and charging the {$95.00} fee. Fast forward, the {$95.00} fee hit my account on XX/XX/19. This is deceptive. 

I budget my expenses on a monthly basis. I planned to pay the {$95.00} annual fee when i performed the upgrade back in XX/XX/XXXX. It is unfair for Chase to secretly place a {$95.00} fee on my account 5 months after performing a transaction. To me, it feels as if they were hoping I wouldn't notice, not pay my bill, and get charged interest on the fee since it wasn't a planned expense for the month of XX/XX/XXXX. 

Chase did not tell me that the fee would take 5 months before it hit my account. Chase did not email me or call me to let me know that it the fee was posted on XX/XX/XXXX. There was no attempt made to inform me. 

It concerns me that Chase feels that it is appropriate to delay the charging of fees until their customer may not notice it, in hopes of tricking them when they aren't expecting it. 

When I spoke with an agent and then their supervisor, they told me that it could take up to 6 months before an annual fee hits the account when performing a product upgrade. This is not in the terms and conditions or visible on a product page or in any of the communications. 

This should not be allowed.

While reaching out to JP Morgan Chase regarding fraudulent activity on my account, caused by a XXXX glitch, the physical credit card was cancelled with the intention of sending me a new card. I have been a happy customer of Chase for over 10 years prior to this situation. 

On XX/XX/2018 at approximately XXXX EST, before a new card was received, I was called by the JP Morgan Chase Collections department to discuss a 'Hardship ' arrangement to pay off the outstanding balance on the account. I spoke with the representative regarding the program and its benefits/pitfalls. During her disclosures I specifically asked, " Will this program 'Suspend ' my account ( meaning I would be able to use the account once it was in good standings ) or 'Close ' my account ( meaning I would have to re-apply for a credit card once my credit score was acceptable ). '' The representative quoted 'Suspend ' and in doing so I agreed to the terms of the 'Hardship ' arrangement.

In an attempt to purchase my first home I went to get pre-approved for a mortgage loan only to find out my credit score was so low that I couldn't be approved even with a co-signer. I requested more information and was told that my credit score no longer showed a 'JP Morgan Chase Credit Card XXXX ' With the hopes of getting more information, I reached out to Chase directly.

Initially Chase could not pull up my account because the card number I was using for verification had been cancelled and they had no record of the account ( Chase updated my account to show a card number I had yet to receive ). Once I verified my identity I was informed that : 1 ) It is company policy to 'Close ' the account when a customer enters into a 'Hardship ' arrangement EVEN IF a representative falsely claimed the account would be 'Suspended ' 2 ) There was no recourse to my account getting closed without my informed consent.

3 ) Chase does not provide copies of audio recordings or transcripts, they are for 'quality assurance purposes only ' and are 'Chase property, ' despite the fact that customers have to agree to be recorded to begin with.

4 ) Chase does not mail out contract agreement information, documents regarding the 'Hardship ' arrangement, or 'Right of first refusal ' forms.

In the last two weeks I have been repeatedly turned down when requesting an audio recording or text transcript of the conversation where I was offered the 'Hardship ' arrangement. 

Due to a lack of recourse I requested the 'Legal ' department or an address/name of someone I could send a formal request to. I ended up going through several departments with very little success until another Chase supervising rep ( ID : XXXX ) gave me the 'National Subpoena Processing ' address to request the audio recording.

After numerous complaints to and requests for information through the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau regarding fraudulent transactions processed at a Branch Banking & Trust ( BB & T ), I have obtained documents demonstrating that BB & T opened at least one fraudulent joint account in my name without my authorization, knowledge, physical presence, or valid identification. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, BB & T opened a joint account ending in XXXX in my name at its XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, VA XXXX location. I was not physically present for this as I was serving as a XXXX XXXX XXXX in rural XXXX and BB & T transactions from my personal checking account ending in XXXX confirm that I made a withdrawal in XXXX, XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. I did not know of or authorize the opening of the joint account ending in XXXX. The account signature card dates my forged signature as XX/XX/XXXX. I was, again, serving abroad and did not sign this document at any time. Furthermore, as I learned over the phone from BB & T 's Identity Theft unit, BB & T accepted a voided and therefore invalidated Colorado drivers license as proof of my identity. I would like to note that this license literally has holes punched through it spelling " VOID '' and that I had maintained a Virginia drivers license for years prior to XX/XX/XXXX. 

This is in direct violation of FDIC Law, Regulations, Related Acts mandates in Miscellaneous Statutes and Regulations Part 1020 that banks must have a Consumer Identification Program ( CIP ) that contains procedures for verifying the identity of the customer, using information obtained in accordance with paragraph ( a ) ( 2 ) ( i ) of this section, within a reasonable time after the account is opened. Appropriate documents from an individual may include an unexpired government-issued identification evidencing nationality or residence and bearing a photograph or similar safeguard, such as a driver 's license or passport. As outlined above, BB & T accepted no such document. When a person other than an individual ( such as a corporation, partnership, or trust ) opens an account, the FDIC requires documents showing the existence of the entity, such as certified articles of incorporation, a government-issued business license, a partnership agreement, or trust instrument. At no time did I consent to or issue a trust instrument to another individual. 

The FDIC allots for verification through non-documentary methods and the bank 's non-documentary procedures must address situations where an individual is unable to present an unexpired government-issued identification document that bears a photograph or similar safeguard ; the bank is not familiar with the documents presented ; the account is opened without obtaining documents ; the customer opens the account without appearing in person at the bank ; and where the bank is otherwise presented with circumstances that increase the risk that the bank will be unable to verify the true identity of a customer through documents. I have not been provided with any evidence that BB & T pursued non-documentary verification as it maintained an invalidated drivers license as proof of my identity in relation to the joint account. 

This fraudulently-opened joint account ending in XXXX was used to deposit a check in my name on XX/XX/XXXX. This check, numbered XXXX, was in the amount of {$20000.00}. BB & T records confirm that I received a total of {$4000.00} from check number XXXX through a phone transfer from account ending in XXXX to account ending in XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. I was not aware that these funds were from a fraudulent joint account nor that they were from a check reissued under false pretenses in the amount of {$20000.00}. 

The joint account ending in XXXX was closed on XX/XX/XXXX without my awareness of its existence while I remained in XXXX. A closing balance of {$10000.00} was issued to the individual who closed the account. I did not receive this money. 

I am demanding an explanation as to how the account ending in XXXX was opened, acknowledgement of fraud, and swift reimbursement of check number XXXX. Additionally, I am demanding to know how many other accounts ( aside from those ending in XXXX and XXXX ) were opened in my name at BB & T and all correlating records. I would not be making these demands if BB & T had adhered to FDIC regulations and believe that the bank should be held accountable to the full extent of the law.

Hi, Thank you for your time helping us with this. 

In XXXX of XXXX my husband and I noticed XXXX charges on my debit card for XXXX and XXXX that we did not make. 

XX/XX/XXXX - XXXX {$260.00} XX/XX/XXXX - XXXX XXXX {$400.00} Upon contacting Bank of America regarding the purchases they cancelled the card, issued another, and began a fraud investigation. Shortly thereafter, they credited our account for both the amounts totaling {$670.00}. We did not hear back from them until the beginning of XX/XX/XXXX when they sent us a letter saying that the fraud claim had been resolved and no error had occurred ( See attached BofA_Fraud_Resolution_Letter ). They subsequently withdrew the amounts back out of our bank account. ( Note the wording " error '' of the letter. Fraud is not an error. ) I contacted Bank of America regarding this issue to find out why the case had been reversed and they told me that one charge was confirmed as fraudulent XXXX XXXX XXXX. Then they proceeded to tell me that both were then denied because we physically shopped at both XXXX and XXXX XXXX before, because there were a number of days in between the charges and us noticing them, because we had logged into our account around the same time, and because no attempt was made to drain the account. Frustrated, I began questioning them on their investigation practices and learned that they use a third party " back office investigators '' and could not tell me what steps were taken during the investigation. They also told me that the federal government didn't allow them to investigate further so they " had to deny '' the claim. 

After speaking with a representative at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I began a little bit of research on my own in order to provide as much information as I could for this report. Upon contacting XXXX XXXX I found that only the XXXX purchases that I made in the summer of XXXX in person in XXXX XXXX, AZ showed under my account name. Thus confirming my card was used for a purchase which happened under another account name. 

Bringing this to BofA 's attention they suggested I submit a faxed letter stating the findings and requesting that the case be reopened. ( See attached BofAFraudLetter XXXX. I did so and on XX/XX/XXXX called and confirmed that the case had been reopened. 

Not having seen nor heard anything since, I obtained my old card number from the bank and once again contacted both XXXX and XXXX XXXX regarding the charges. 
The woman at XXXX XXXX said she had just had the same experience and suggested I contact the Atty General in this matter. She was able to confirm for me that the account holders name, address, and phone number were not mine because they did not match the billing information that I gave her. She was able to tell me that the purchase was of a XXXX amp circular saw work bench. 

Next, I contacted XXXX and went through the same process with the gentleman there. I was able to learn that the purchase was for a XXXX 60 volt maximum lithium ion battery. I was also able to deduce that the account holders name, address, and phone number were not the same as mine, yet again. Then I learned that the last name of the purchaser was XXXX of which, I know none. 

Finally, I contacted BofA again today only to find that the case had been once again closed for the same reasons as before. The investigators failing to do their due diligence or choosing to not pursue the case further, instead allowing Bank of America to steal the money from me rather than the responsible parties. 

I learned that XXXX XXXX and XXXX both would pay the amounts to Bank of America if the case was proven then would have to pursue a suit against the perpetrators to recover their losses. Also, the personal information of the perpetrator is not available to the victim by law, however, it is available to the investigators and Bank of America. 

I respectfully request this issue be investigated in order to right the wrong that has happened and return our money that we did not spend. 

Again, thank you for your time in this matter.

state: I applied for a Bank of America checking account back in XX/XX/XXXX. They stated they could not open a bank account for me based off of credit information. In XX/XX/XXXX, I had a check from a settlement for a personal injury that had happened and I was told I couldn't cash it at XXXX and I had to take it to the bank. So XX/XX/XXXX I went to Bank of America to cash the check and they told me I couldn't cash it that I needed to deposit it, so I did. It was for {$29000.00}, so I split half to the checking half in savings. Because I had earlier received a small PUA backpayment I was still living fine off of that and I just was going to wait until I needed the BOA money to use it. I went to the atm the same day to try to make sure the money was in it through the atm with the virtual card. It was so i left. So, from XX/XX/XXXX until XX/XX/XXXX, i then called XXXX because I waited for my card in the mail and because the person I live with went to jail, and there was a no contact order in place, i couldn't go and get the mailbox key from him/jail. So I contacted Bank of America and explained my situation, and asked if instead of having a debit card sent to my home, considering the circumstances, if I could come in and pick XXXX up she stated no and stated she would be sending out a different debit card. So by then I'd say it was around XXXX XXXX or so that I finally received the debit card by waiting outside and ahowing the deliverywoman my ID and asked if i could please have the mail and at that moment she did, .and I was excited. I activated it and left it on my dresser drawer in my bedroom. It was going good until a woman asked me to run her to XXXX for gas money and I figured okay and I did. But then when she got of of my vehicle I noticed my little pocket book and phone were missing. And because she was in a motel I wasn't sure what room she was in because she got out of the car so quick and I just drove Away. I XXXX have dropped her off and noticed about XXXX mins after that my things were missing. I hadn't realized she asked me to use the phone, and i let her. I panicked and was furious at the same time because she had taken the phone and my money and because when I went home I realized I had no card, to call in order to get the statements and ask them to freeze the card. So I had to wait until I was around a phone to call and tell them what happened and to put a freeze on the account. I contacted the bank and explained the issue and that there was no way any one can go through {$29000.00} in a matter of a month. So then I looked more into my statements around XXXX XXXX and I noticed alot of " back to back '' charges that I was concerned about so I went to the Acutral B.O.A location and explained to the woman, XXXX, the situation and she decided to close the account, and open a new one. Because it showed {$3800.00} overdrafted I had no choice but to open the second account, so if I had deposits they would go to the new one. There were a few temporary credits added back to the old account, expect becaue it was overdrafted, i had to fix the balance on the account first and if any money left would go to the new account. I filed the first claim for {$8400.00}, and XXXX asked about a few more transactions that looked to be unauthorized in which they were. It was around {$3400.00}. So she opened that new account told me to wait until I received my new card in mail and someone will be in contact with me reguarding the issues because she, herself could not do anything besides have it looked into. So a few days went by and I went back in to BOA to see what was going on, and I did this for about a month. I still to this day was railroaded and told different things by different employers because if I called BOA employees were almost lost to what I was stating and I still haven't had any luck to this day. The only excuse they gave me was, that the transactions were authorized by me or by someone I know. And I explained why that was incorrect and the banker, XXXX XXXX never returned any of my calls and just sent a packet of statements to my house. I, still to this day, have tried calling and figuring.it out but there was a point that when I did call, it goes straight to her business voice-mail.

In XX/XX/XXXX, I was referred to XXXX XXXX XXXX because I wanted to trade-in a car that I was financing. Due to my " poor '' credit, I was told that they would definitely get me into a better car with better terms. 

On XX/XX/XXXX I went there and spent hours with mostly the salesperson and then going back and forth with the finance manager. My trade-in was appraised ( excellent condition and low mileage for a car that age ). I was led to believe that XXXX XXXX  XXXX was taking my trade-in. After all, the reason why I bothered to go there in the first place. I was anticipating slightly lower payments and/or a better car and deal. 

As I began reading, listening to the salesman and finance manager, as well as going back and forth signing the paperwork, I asked them what about my trade-in. That's when I was told that I was " upside down on my loan ''. I did not know what that meant, so they explained it to me. I asked why I was not told that before. I also asked, " what am I supposed to do with two cars? ". The salesperson said that I need to find a way to get rid of it. 

This situation made me feel absolutely helpless. I went to the dealership in an attempt to not only get my finances better situated, but to also build my credit. I believe that I was taken advantage of. They exercised aggressive sales tactics and blatantly lied about taking my trade-in. As a single mother with only my small income to support my family, I struggled tremendously trying to pay two car notes and the insurance. I was placed in extreme financial distress. In addition, I also came to realize that based on my situation at the time it is highly unlikely that someone with my income would even qualify for that particular loan. 

This loan has caused me financial turmoil. On XX/XX/XXXX, Santander Consumer USA reported this account as a chargeoff. I can not improve my credit, which prevents me from being able to reach my goals of a better life for my family. Upon recently researching my concern, I have realized that I am a victim of predatory lending.

state: I have an FHA mortgage with Freedom Mortgage Corporation that was temporarily on a Covid-19 forbearance. XX/XX/2021, I called Freedom Mortgage and indicated that I wanted to remove the loan from forbearance and resume payments via an owner occupied modification. Additionally, in XX/XX/2021, I resumed my regular monthly mortgage payments and of note, I have been making my regular monthly mortgage payments, every single month since XX/XX/2021. During this XXXX call, to end my forbearance, I was told that I would receive a loan modification packet within 30 days from underwriting with new terms of my mortgage and my signature would be required to accept this offer. Unfortunately, 4 months later, I never received this packet, and my mortgage is still in forbearance and no one at Freedom Mortgage has been able to help me move my mortgage into a current status after 4 months of waiting for loan modification documents. I call weekly and I do not get any clear information and it quite frustrating and concerning to me. There so many disparities in the knowledge levels in the customer service reps and Freedom has these escalation supervisor and their ability to triage and follow-up on escalated issues is sub-par. My property is held in a land trust and I have sent in the required Land Trust Review and a certified copy of my trust agreement to show that I am the only vested owner on my deed. Can your organization please intervene, regulate, or help enforce a level of fairness and diligence in business operations and efficiencies at Freedom with this situation? This forbearance being reported on my credit report 4 months later after I indicated I am able to pay my mortgage is totally unethical and just irresponsible and there is no one accountable within the entire company to even help me. Overall, Freedom Mortgage has been a very difficult company to work with in general. I can not recommend this company at all.

Detailed Summary : This writer ( XXXX ) settled a debt with XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX in the amount of {$130.00}. The full debt price was documented as {$210.00}, however upon speaking with a representative from their company via phone XXXX was told by the representative that the debt could be settled and considered PAID IN FULL if the agreed upon amount of {$130.00} was paid. XXXX agreed to the settlement amount of {$130.00}. XXXX received documentation from XXXX XXXX XXXX  dated XX/XX/XXXX stating the account was paid in full. 

XXXX received a letter from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( RPM ) dated XX/XX/XXXX regarding owing the debt amount of {$210.00} to XXXX. This writer contacted XXXX  and explained to the representative that XXXX had previously paid the debt to another company and settled for the amount of {$130.00}. As advised by the representative XXXX sent proof of payment ( redacted bank statement as advised by the representative on the phone ) via email to XXXX  and was told this writer would hear back from XXXX within 30 days. XXXX did not hear back from any representative of the company at all. 
XXXX received a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX stating that " in the last quarter, XXXX received the following payment of {$130.00} on XX/XX/XXXX. All payments received this quarter have been applied to the account placed with XXXX ; however, this account is now closed in our office. '' XXXX received another letter from XXXX stating there was still an outstanding of {$210.00} on the XXXX account. XXXX reached out to XXXX and spoke to a representative. The representative named XXXX stated to this writer to fax the documentation of proof of payment to the number she provided and call back the following Monday to ensure she received it. XXXX complied, faxed the information the very next morning and waited until Monday morning to call back. Upon calling the given number back this writer was not connected with XXXX and was told my the representative on the phone that it would take up to 30 days for XXXX to sort and review the faxed information sent. 

XXXX again received a letter from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( RPM ) dated XX/XX/XXXX stating that XXXX  was willing to accept 40 % ( {$84.00} ) of the total due ( {$210.00} ) to satisfy the outstanding balance. The supervisor stated that the information sent was not valid proof and that additional information ( receipts ) needed to be sent in as proof. The supervisor also stated that someone from XXXX would be reaching out within 30 days upon receiving new information that was sent in. XXXX again complied and sent the additional documentation to the email address XXXX  provided. As of XX/XX/XXXX XXXX has yet to have heard back from XXXX. 

XXXX recently received another letter from another letter from a new company called Diversified Adjustment Service Inc. ( DAS ) dated XX/XX/XXXX that stated " your account has been placed with us for collection in the amount f {$210.00}. XXXX then scanned and emailed all of the previous letters and correspondence from the other companies attempting to collect the debt along with proof of payment and emailed it to Diversified Adjustment Service Inc. Upon sending the email XXXX contact DAS via phone and spoke to a representative. He stated that the information has not been processed yet and to call back by Friday to check if it was in DAS ' system. XXXX stated that a call would be made on Friday to check into the situation. 

Resolution : XXXX would like all of the agencies attempting to collect this debt to seize all forms of contact/ communication ( phone, email, letter, socials media and any other form of communication that may apply ) and would like the debt absolved and removed from collection, personal credit report ( if applicable ), presented and closed as a paid in full account.

I am fortunate to work for a company that has agreed to assist with my student loan payments. For them to do so, I am required to submit a copy of a current billing statement. One might imagine that this would be a simple request for Aidvantage to fulfill ; but the past month or so that I've spent trying to contact them to secure this document seems to suggest otherwise ( and also seems to reflect a larger, more concerning trend of incompetence and complete lack of ability to effectively service their " customers '' ). The following paragraphs contain a brief rundown of events : On XX/XX/XXXX I received email correspondence from the U.S. Department of Education with information about preparing for the continuation of student loan payments. In this email, I was advised that I could expect to receive a current billing statement from Aidvantage at least 21 days before my payment is due ( XX/XX/XXXX ). Upon receipt of this message, I registered an account online with Aidvantage, and took care to ensure that all of my personal information was correct and up to date to ensure that there would be no issue in receiving further communication from the lender. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email from Aidvantage which indicated that they were to have started sending out billing statements on XX/XX/XXXX. I had not gotten anything in the mail by that point, so I waited for a few days to accommodate mail delivery service times. A week later, on XX/XX/XXXX, I still had not received any correspondence, so I attempted to call Aidvantage customer service during regular business hours in hopes of getting some kind of update. I sat on hold for over an hour before needing to get on with my day, so no contact was made. 

Later that day, I logged back on to my account to see whether any of this information was available for me to access electronically. It was not. I did, however, notice that Aidvantage advertised a Live Chat feature built into their website, which presumably would connect me to someone who may be able to assist with my request. But when I tried to use this feature, I was met with an error message which prevented me from making any kind of contact. I figured that there was some kind of technical issue going on, and resolved to give them a couple of days to fix it before trying again. 

The following day, XX/XX/XXXX, I received another email from Aidvantage with the subject line : " Your monthly billing statement is ready. '' I opened the email and saw that it contained a link that said " View Statement. '' This was great news -- problem solved, right? But when I clicked on the link, I was directed to a broken webpage that did not allow me locate any useful information ( I've attached a screenshot of the page that I took this evening. It's still broken ). I tried again to call customer service and utilize the non-functional chat feature, neither of which yielded any kind of response. At this point, I'm starting to wonder whether this company actually has anyone working for them On XX/XX/XXXX, I had a bit more time to spare, so I tried to call in again. I waited on hold for nearly 2 hours this time before giving up, and checked the website again to see if the Live Chat function was back online. I repeated this process over the next several days ( with varying hold times ) while keeping a close eye on my physical mailbox in hopes that I would still receive a statement as promised. No success. 

Fast forward a bit, and it's XX/XX/XXXX, and my payment is due in less than 2 weeks, and I still haven't gotten any information or communication from Aidvantage. Everything is still broken. Incredibly frustrated, I started combing through their website to find any kind of useful information. I finally located a link that would allow me to email their customer service team, so I did. Upon submitting my request, I received an automated email which advised that I could expect a response within 1-2 business days. It's been about 5 business days, and I still have yet to hear back. 

Today, XXXX, I found myself stuck in traffic, so I decided to try calling customer service again. I wasn't hopeful, but it's become apparent to me that my options here are pretty limited. After an hour, I was finally connected to a representative. 

I spoke with the gentleman on the other line, and repeated my original request for a billing statement. He was a nice guy, but didn't seem to have a clue as to what I was actually looking for. It took me about 15 minutes of explaining, but he was finally able to confirm what I was needing and let me know that a copy of a statement will be mailed to me within the next 5-7 business days. I asked whether he could just send me an email instead, but he advised that would not be possible. Doesn't make a ton of sense to me, but I didn't bother asking why. I was mostly just happy to discover that Aidvantage actually has employees. 

Now, assuming that a billing statement has actually been placed in the mail and I can actually expect to receive it this time ; I will not be able to access it or submit it my employer until after my first payment is XXXX XXXX XXXX. My recent interactions ( or attempts thereof ) with Aidvantage have not inspired confidence that they will actually follow through on their commitment, which is why I wanted to ensure that a formal complaint was documented. 

I know that this is a relatively minor issue, but if my recent experience is indicative of " the norm '' in dealing with this company, then I can only imagine what other customers have had to go through while preparing for repayment. The financial stress of repayment is enough of a burden on the consumers, and it's only been magnified by Aidvantage 's utter lack of care or respect for their clients. Frankly, I'm amazed that this firm has been allowed to take on the responsibility of administering something so impactful to the lives of thousands ( millions? ) of people. I'm not sure whether there is a standard of care for these kinds of organizations, but I'm certain that Aidvantage has no interest in establishing or adhering to it.

Also, the Live Chat is still broken.

On XX/XX/year> I ordered XXXX XXXX lamps from XXXX XXXX, with a place of business noted on their website as XXXX, XXXX. The lamps cost {$920.00}. The vendor did not offer any type of insurance for the purchase. This seemed like a very small operation and I was reluctant to order from them until I discovered that payment would be made through PayPal, which I expected would be a fair arbiter should problems arise. 

The lamps were received on XX/XX/year> from an address in XXXX. They were left at in front of my house by the delivery carrier. The package was damaged and the packaging was completely inadequate for shipping such easily damaged items by international carrier. All three lamps were dented, and one had a piece broken off. The lamps were unusable. 

On XX/XX/year> I emailed the vendor asking for a refund and offering to return the items if the vendor supplied a return shipping label. 

I did not receive a response to the email so I sent another email on XX/XX/year> with the same information. 

I sent a third email on XX/XX/year>. 

On XX/XX/XXXX I was offered replacement items if I paid shipping cost, the amount of which was not disclosed. This was an unsatisfactory offer. As I was not responsible for the inadequate packing that resulted in damage and as the seller did not offer insurance at the time of original purchase, I did not feel that I should bear the cost of the sellers negligence. In addition, given the inadequate packaging, I was reluctant to encounter the same issue a second time. 

There were many email exchanges over the next few days without the seller offering a substantively different resolution. 

I filed a complaint with PayPal, who had processed the charge, on XX/XX/year>. Through multiple exchanges the seller began to insist that the only resolution was for me to return the items after which I would get a refund of the amount paid. I was also required to return the items to XXXX rather than XXXX where the seller was ostensibly located. However, after checking with XXXX, the estimated cost of shipping to XXXX was {$1500.00}! The original purchase was {$920.00}. Therefore I was being asked to pay {$1500.00} to get a return of my initial {$920.00}. 

On XX/XX/year>, when it became clear that the seller was not willing to take any responsibility for the negligent packaging that resulted in the damage, I escalated to a claim with PayPal. The seller kept making the same offer, a full refund of {$920.00} after I paid about {$1500.00} to return the items. I continued to respond that this was unacceptable. At XXXX point, PayPal asked me to accept or reject the offer. When I tried to respond, the only option I was given was to complete a form with return shipping information. Without shipping information, the form could not be submitted so there was no way to again indicate that the offer was not acceptable. In the notes section of the form, I explained that I was not accepting the offer and that I put in a tracking number of all zeroes and a carrier ID of No Carrier to be able to submit the form but that, in fact, I was not sending the item back. 

I even followed up with another note to the complaint file a few days later reconfirming that I was not accepting the offer and was not returning the items. 

PayPal closed the case in the sellers favor because I did not return the items. Not once in the entire string of messages did PayPal ever acknowledge that it made no sense to pay {$1500.00} to get {$920.00} back and, furthermore, this situation was completely the fault of the merchant who was taking no responsibility for the situation. 

On XX/XX/year>, I called PayPal to discuss the case and to have them address the fact that not once did they acknowledge the lunacy of the sellers offer that would have cost me more money than I would have gotten back. When the customer service representative could not help, she transferred me to a supervisor. The supervisor kept repeating that I did not get a refund because I did not return the item. I repeatedly kept asking him to explain to me how it made sense for me to spend an additional {$1500.00} to get {$920.00} back. He never once answered the question. He just kept repeating the need to have returned the item. 

At my request, he promised me a call back from another supervisor that same day. Now, XXXX hours later, I have not received a call back from PayPal. 

My complaint with PayPal is that they did not attempt to adjudicate this situation in good faith. They kept repeating the sellers request that I ship the items back at my expense to receive a refund without acknowledging that the shipping costs, that the seller would not reimburse, were more than the cost of the items that would presumably be returned to me. PayPal never addressed my multiple comments about a proposed resolution that would have cost me more than doing nothing and losing my {$920.00}. Despite multiple requests PayPal did not explain the logic of the proposed resolution which, of course, did not make any sense. They failed in their duty to adjudicate my claim in good faith, siding instead with an unreasonable seller and never responding to an explanation of how the proposed resolution was fair.

state:
On Monday, XX/XX/2021, I was contacted by Wells Fargo via text message asking if XXXX specific charges were authorized by me. After responding to the text, I received another text showing a debit to my checking account, also not authorized by me. I immediately called Wells Fargo and told them that my account had clearly been hacked and to shut down my checking and savings accounts with them. 

After watching several more transactions being deducted from my account via text alerts on my phone, I was informed from the customer representative to whom I was speaking that your company actually had video footage of a man at a Wells Fargo ATM machine in XXXX XXXX Texas, withdrawing money from my account matching the time stamp of the withdrawal from my account. I live and was in XXXX at this time with the ONLY debit card issued on this account in my possession. Also, I am the ONLY authorized user on my account. 

When trying to get into my account while on the phone with the bank, I discovered that my password had been changed thereby locking me out of my own account. Upon further discussion with your representative, I was told that someone had called the bank and verbally requested {$4000.00} be transferred from my savings account, which they willingly did without my approval or verification. 

When asked to see the photos of the man at the Wells Fargo ATM and hear the phone recording of the call when Wells Fargo transferred my money in my savings account to my checking account, I was refused. 

On the Wells Fargo website, it says to Contact us immediately if you suspect fraud on your account ( XXXX ) or you responded to a suspicious email, text message, or phone call. When you call, we will review your accounts, identify all unauthorized transactions, and help keep your accounts secure. 

I did so in my call telling them that NONE of the transactions made on XX/XX/2021 were made OR authorized by me, and they failed miserably in keeping my XXXX  secure as many transactions continued to be made that day. They actually assisted the thief when your company allowed a phone request of a transfer of {$4000.00} from my savings account into my checking account with NO notification to or verification from me. These large purchase amounts and the location from where they occurred do not match up with my normal daily account activity. 

Furthermore, I was also NOT notified by the company when the person changed my password on my account. However, when I did this after this theft, I immediately got an email from Wells Fargo telling me that my password had been changed. On XXXX of my countless phone calls to Wells Fargo, all of my account information was verified as correct. Why did I not receive an email telling me that my password had been changed by the person stealing from me but did when I completed this action? 

Their website says that they protect my data by doing the following : XXXX XXXX XXXX We are helping to keep your money safe by monitoring your accounts and XXXX contact you if we detect unusual activity. If it's not your purchase, we will help you resolve it. We use various methods to contact our customers including email, text, push notification from the mobile app, or phone call. When we contact you, we will not ask for your card PIN, access code, or your online banking password. 
If your banking behavior differs from your usual activity, we XXXX send you an access code to confirm your identity, prevent certain types of transactions, or restrict account access ( including card declines ). Further proof of identity XXXX be required before we restore online access. 

The website goes on to say that customers are covered with account protections by stating the following : Unauthorized Account Activity Under federal law, Regulation XXXX ( Electronic Fund Transfer Act ) provides certain protections to consumer customers when there is unauthorized account activity. Regulation XXXX covers transfers of funds through electronic methods such as, the use of a debit or credit card, ATM withdrawals, and direct deposit activity through a checking, savings, or other consumer asset account at a financial institution used primarily for personal, family, or household purposes. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX Wells Fargo XXXX and XXXX XXXX come with XXXX Liability XXXX at no extra cost. You wont be held responsible for unauthorized transactions, so long as you report them promptly. 

Based on the companys promises, they failed to protect my data AND have NOT covered my account protections even though I notified them IMMEDIATELY when debits to my account showed up on my phone. 

Once again, not only did they not protect me, the account holder ; they assisted the person who stole a combined total of {$4600.00} from my checking and savings accounts. I was told that my money would be returned to my accounts in totality within XXXX business days. That deadline passed on XX/XX/XXXX, and I still have not received my money that was taken from my accounts. I have also not been communicated with and have had to initiate communication with your company in order to find if any progress, or lack thereof, has been made regarding my case. And when I do talk with someone, nobody knows the facts of my case, and Ive had to repeat the events multiple times. And at the end of each conversation, nobody has offered any solutions to the problem. 

When I called the bank on XX/XX/2021, the last day of their own aforementioned timeline, I was told that my claim had been denied because of authorization by me of these transactions. That is complete and utter nonsense based on the proof that I gave in my phone call to you on XX/XX/2021 as well as their own admitted video footage of someone taking money from my account via a Wells Fargo ATM. There is also a phone recording of the person asking for the transfer of {$4000.00} from my savings account to my checking. 

In short, Wells Fargo has failed me at every single turn, and did not upheld their promises to me as a customer nor your protection of my money.
